The command was read from the Book sent with truth — *bi-al-ḥaqq* — to judge by what He shows (4:105): to follow desire is to judge by what He did not show.

**If You Distort or Refuse — He Is All-Aware**

The threat *wa in talwū aw tuʿriḍū fa inna Allāha kāna bi-mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — and if you distort, twist, the testimony, or refuse, turn away from giving it, then indeed God is ever All-Aware of what you do — was explained with two evasions: *talwū* — to twist, bend the tongue, change wording, give ambiguous testimony — and *tuʿriḍū* — to turn aside, refuse, neglect to testify, hide. Both are the opposite of standing for justice and witnessing for God. The sūrah has exposed those who hide from people while God is with them where they plot by night (4:108) — twisting is the daylight form of that night plotting — and those who advocate in this life but will find no advocate on the Day (4:109) — refusing is that advocate's silence where truth was needed. *God is ever All-Aware of what you do* was explained as that He who is Fully Aware, encompassing everything (4:126), and All-Aware where settlement was sought (4:128), and All-Hearing, All-Seeing where both rewards are with Him (4:134), knows twisting and refusing as He knows standing. The promise that *whoever does good, male or female, with faith will enter Paradise, not wronged a speck* (4:124) assumes the testimony that admits good; to twist it is to wrong the speck.

**A Verse That Follows Universal Ownership With Universal Justice**

Placed after the string of universal addresses — We commanded those before you and you to be mindful (4:131); to Him belongs all, He suffices as Trustee (4:132); He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133); with Him are both rewards, He hears and sees (4:134) — this verse is the believers' answer: stand firm for justice as witnesses for Him. The sūrah that began with honouring ties from a single soul (4:1), that showed orphan girls deprived yet desired (4:127), the wife fearing ill-conduct where settlement is best (4:128), wives between whom inclination cannot be equalled (4:129), now says standing for justice may be against the very ties you honour — yourselves, parents, kin — and may favour or deny the rich or poor — yet do not follow desire to deviate, lest you twist or turn away. The sūrah that taught verification before fighting (4:94) and judgment by the Book (4:105) here teaches verification before testifying: be ever-standing, so that twisting and refusing are not options. For the weak this is the highest protection: where wealth tempts and poverty pities, justice upheld for God is a haven as sure as the emigrant's many havens — and He who is All-Aware of what you do will not wrong a speck.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:136

> O believers! Have faith in Allah, His Messenger, the Book He has revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before. Indeed, whoever denies Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray

**O Believers — Have Faith in God, the Messenger, and the Books**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū āminū bi Allāhi wa rasūlihi wa al-kitābi alladhī nazzala ʿalā rasūlihi wa al-kitābi alladhī anzala min qablu* — O you who believe, have faith in God and His Messenger, and the Book He sent down upon His Messenger, and the Scripture He sent down before. *Āminū* addressed to *those who believed* was explained not as contradiction but as command to firmness, renewal, and comprehensiveness: those who already believe are told to remain believers, to increase in belief, to believe without distinction — as the sūrah has shown that those who believe and do good are admitted to Gardens (4:57, 4:122), yet belief must be in the full articles. *In God and His Messenger* was read as the two taught inseparably, where obeying the Messenger is obeying God (4:80), messengers are sent to be obeyed by His leave (4:64), and the Messenger is taken as judge without resistance (4:65). *The Book He sent down upon His Messenger* was explained as the Qur'an, sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105), whose word none exceeds in truth (4:122). *And the Scriptures He sent down before* was read as the Books given before — the Torah and Gospel in their revealed form — matching *worship God alone, associate none* (4:36) and *We commanded those given the Scripture before you, and you, to be mindful* (4:131) — the command is one. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book claim by wish (4:123) and distort words (4:46); to believe in the Books before is to believe in them as revealed, before distorting hands altered them — not to follow altered claims.

**And Whoever Denies — Has Gone Far Astray**

The threat *wa man yakfur bi Allāhi wa malāʾikatihī wa kutubihī wa rusulihī wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri fa qad ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — whoever denies God, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray — was explained with the five articles. *Yakfur* — to deny, cover — was read as the denial that makes association unforgiven (4:116) and following other than the believers' path end in burning (4:115). The five — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — are the Book's summary of faith. Angels were read as the recorders of night schemes (4:81), the takers of souls asked *what were you doing?* (4:97), the witnesses beside the guarded prayer (4:102); to deny angels is to deny those realities. Books and messengers were read as the conveyors of the Book in truth and wisdom taught (4:113); the Last Day as the Day about which there is no doubt, where all will be gathered (4:87) and where hypocrites and disbelievers will be gathered in Hell (4:140). *Ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — gone far astray — was linked to going far after guidance became clear (4:115); denial of these articles after clarity is the farthest distance, because it denies the very witnesses who prove the clarity.

**A Verse That Follows Justice With Creed**

Placed after *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves, rich or poor; do not follow desire; if you twist or turn away, He is All-Aware* (4:135), this verse follows justice with the creed that secures it. The sūrah has traversed judging by the Book (4:105), the rule of secret talks (4:114), defiance of the Messenger (4:115), association far astray (4:116), the female gods and Satan's share (4:117–118), Satan's orders and delusion (4:119–120), the two true abodes (4:121–122), grace not by wishes (4:123), good with faith not wronged a speck (4:124), best faith as submission following Abraham, whom God took as friend (4:125), ownership and encompassing (4:126), instruction for orphan women and helpless children (4:127), settlement best though greed persists (4:128), imperfect emotional justice yet no total inclining (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130), the universal charge to be mindful though He is Self-Sufficient (4:131), sufficiency as Trustee (4:132), capability to replace humanity (4:133), and both rewards with Him, All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) — now faith in the full articles is named as the root that makes justice possible without twisting. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by desire (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here names the content desire most attacks — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — after which far straying is the fruit.

**Belief Commanded to Believers — Renewal, Not Repetition**

The command *O you who believe, have faith* was explained as renewal, firming, and widening: to believers who believed in part — in God but not the Messenger; in this Book but not those before; in God and Books but not angels or the Last Day — the command is to believe entirely, without making distinction between God and His messengers, as those do who say *we believe in some and disbelieve in others, seeking a compromise* (4:150). The sūrah has shown that such distinction is the compromisers' denial; here the command closes it: have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before — with angels and the Last Day implied — no selecting. Where the sūrah next says *those who believed then disbelieved, then believed, then increased in disbelief — He will neither forgive nor guide* (4:137), wavering belief is shown as fragile where the articles are not firm; *āminū* here is the firming before that warning.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Law in the Last Day**

Though a list of articles, the verse anchors law in the Last Day. The justice just commanded — standing though against selves and parents, not distorting — has no motive without the Last Day, where this life's advocates find no advocate before God (4:109) and where hypocrites and disbelievers are gathered in Hell (4:140). To deny the Last Day after clear guidance makes *recompensed accordingly* for evil (4:123) unintelligible; to deny the Books and messengers makes judging by what He shows (4:105) unintelligible; to deny the angels makes the recording of night schemes (4:81, 4:108) unintelligible. For the weak this is the lightest anchoring: to have faith — renewed and entire — in the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) who owns the heavens and earth (4:132) and will not wrong a speck (4:124), is to entrust justice to the Trustee who suffices — the Self-Sufficient who does not need.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:137

> Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed and again disbelieved—˹only˺ increasing in disbelief—Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Way

**Those Who Believed, Then Disbelieved — Then Increased**

The verse states *inna alladhīna āmanū thumma kafarū thumma āmanū thumma kafarū thumma izdādū kufrā* — indeed those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief, adding disbelief. *Believed then disbelieved*, repeated, was explained as oscillation, not mere lapse: belief, then denial, then return to belief, then denial again — not the repentance accepted soon after error (4:17), but performance — hypocrisy's rhythm. *Thumma izdādū kufrā* — then increased in disbelief — was read as that the second disbelief is not a return to the first level but an increase: association after straying (4:116), taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119), invoking female gods (4:117) — each step adds. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than the believers' path is left to what he chose (4:115), and whoever associates has gone far astray (4:116); to oscillate between belief and denial after clarity is to defy after clarity repeatedly — guidance not made firm. Early reports linked the verse to those who wavered between faiths under pressure; the generality was stressed: whoever trades belief for disbelief, and returns only to trade again, increasing, is meant — the hypocrite described as *swaying between this and that, belonging neither to these nor those* (4:143), who seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142).

**Allah Will Neither Forgive Them Nor Guide Them to a Way**

The seal *lam yakun Allāhu li-yaghfira lahum wa lā li-yahdiyahum sabīlā* — Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to a way — was explained with two negations: no forgiveness, no guidance. *To forgive them* was read against the condition attached to *whoever commits evil then seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving* (4.110) — seeking, before death says *now I repent* (4:18); these increase in disbelief instead of seeking, so forgiveness is not sealed. *Nor guide them to a way* was read with *sabīl* — the way — the same way God wills to make clear as noble ways (4:26), that Satan wishes far deviant (4:60), that is the believers' path not to be left (4:115); those who oscillate and increase have closed the way by repeatedly turning. The phrase *will neither forgive* was linked to *He does not forgive association, but forgives what is less* (4:48, 4:116): the increase in disbelief settles into the level where pardon is withheld unless the oscillation is broken by firm belief. The sūrah has said *whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way for him* (4:88) — here the way not found is forgiveness and guidance, because they left it.

**A Verse That Follows Firm Belief With the Portrait of the Unfirm**

Placed after *O believers, have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He sent down upon His Messenger, and the Scriptures He sent down before; whoever denies God, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has gone far astray* (4:136), this verse follows firm belief commanded with unfirm belief described as oscillation. The sūrah has commanded *ever-standing upholders of justice* (4:135), said both rewards are with Him (4:134), and that He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133); oscillation is the opposite of standing: to stand is to remain — to oscillate is to be removed. The sūrah has shown that *had not grace preserved you, they would have deceived you — yet they deceive only themselves* (4:113): oscillation deceives only the self, increasing its disbelief, not harming the Prophet. Where the sūrah will give the hypocrites the news of painful punishment for their alliance with disbelievers (4:138–139) and will forbid sitting with those who deny or ridicule the revelations, else you become like them (4:140), this verse is the theological root: belief, then disbelief, then belief, then increase is the hypocrite's creed.

**Increase in Disbelief After the Light Was Clear**

The phrase *then increased in disbelief* was explained as that disbelief has degrees, as the sūrah's far straying has degrees: to associate is far (4:116); to defy the Messenger after clarity is to be left to stray (4:115); to take Satan as guardian is tremendous, manifest loss (4:119). Increase was linked to making distinction between God and His messengers — believing in some and disbelieving in others, desiring compromise (4:150) — which is itself increase where the compromise comes after clear guidance. The sūrah's arithmetic of good — multiplied many times over (4:40) — has its counterpart in evil's increase: persistence after oscillation does not stay level but adds, as greed adds where not overcome by graciousness (4:128). The seal *will neither forgive nor guide* was therefore read as the consequence of addition: where the return soon after error is pardoned (4:17), increase after oscillation moves the opposite direction — so forgiveness and guidance are withheld.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Hypocrisy Before Its Portrait**

Though brief — *those who believed then disbelieved, then believed again and increased — He will neither forgive nor guide to the Right Way* — the verse anchors hypocrisy before its portrait. Immediately after: *give good news of painful punishment to the hypocrites* (4:138), who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) — portraits of oscillation made alliance. Then: *do not sit with those who deny or ridicule the revelations, else you are like them — He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) — the company of oscillation. Then: *those who wait and watch you, telling each victor, were we not with you?* (4:141) — the waiting of oscillation. All are branches of the wavering that neither forgiveness nor guidance meets (4:137). For the weak this is clarifying: belief is not a wish by which grace is claimed (4:123), nor wavering between sides like those who wait to see what happens (4:141), but firm faith that finds Him All-Forgiving when it seeks after evil (4:110).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:138

> Give good news of a painful punishment to hypocrites

**Give Good News of Painful Punishment to Hypocrites**

The verse states *bashshiri al-munāfiqīna bi-anna lahum ʿadhāban alīmā* — give good news, announce, to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment. *Bashshir* — to give good news — was explained as irony: to announce painful punishment in the idiom of good news, because the hypocrite's own announcements are deceit — they seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142); they show off prayer to be seen (4:142); they wait to see what happens to you and say to whichever side wins, *were we not with you?* (4:141). *Al-munāfiqīn* — hypocrites — was read as those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed again, then increased (4:137); who sway between this and that, belonging to neither (4:143); who will be in the lowest depth of the Fire without helper (4:145). *That for them is a painful punishment* was explained with *alīm* — painful, aching — the same adjective as the Fire prepared for those who consume orphans' wealth (4:10) and for those who persist until death then say *now I repent* (4:18). The sūrah has traced hypocrisy from the community divided into two groups about them (4:88), to the wish that you be alike in disbelief (4:89), to the double-faced who plunge into *fitnah* (4:91), to the lagger who stays and envies (4:72–73), to the plotters by night (4:108); here the announcement is not a warning but a recompense — painful punishment — for the territory between belief and disbelief where they tried to keep both.

**A Verse That Follows Oscillation With Irony**

Placed after *those who believed then disbelieved then increased — He will neither forgive nor guide* (4:137), this verse follows oscillation with irony: the good news for the one who increased in disbelief after believing is painful punishment. The sūrah will say all honour belongs to God (4:139) where hypocrites seek honour from disbeliever allies, and that sitting with those who deny or ridicule the revelations makes you like them, gathered in Hell (4:140); the painful punishment is the announcement for that alliance and that sitting. The sūrah has also shown that the deceitful's night speech displeases Him (4:108) and that advocacy for self-wrongers in this life will find no advocate on the Day (4:109); painful punishment is the Day's answer to the night's delight. Where the sūrah elsewhere says *do not consume wealth unjustly — God is ever Merciful to you* (4:29), yet *whoever does so unjustly, We will burn in a Fire easy for God* (4:30) — easy for Him, painful for them — this announcement is the Fire easy for the One who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133).

**The Good News That Is Not Good**

The verb *bashshir* — give good news — was explained to show that hypocrisy inverts news: what they took as good — advantage with both sides, honour through the company of disbelievers (4:139), safety from you and from their own people while plunging into hostility (4:91) — is announced as painful. The sūrah has said the Devil promises only delusion (4:120) — his good news is delusion; God's *bashshir* here is true news — painful. The contrast was linked to *those who believe and do good, We will admit into Gardens… whose word is more truthful than God's?* (4:122) — the believers' good news is Gardens, true; the hypocrites' good news is painful punishment, true. Classical notes added that *bashshir* for punishment appears where mockery preceded — the hypocrites sat with those who mocked the revelations (4:140) — so the reply answers the mocker with the same idiom, made true.

**A Short Verse That Opens the Hypocrite Portrait**

Though a single sentence — *give good news of painful punishment to the hypocrites* — the verse opens the hypocrite portrait that follows. Immediately: *who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — do they seek honour through them? Surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139) — the portrait of their alliance. Then: *He has already revealed that when you hear the revelations denied or ridiculed, do not sit in that company until they engage in another talk, else you would be like them — He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) — the portrait of their sitting. Then: *those who wait and watch you — if you gain victory from God, they say, were we not with you?* (4:141) — the portrait of their waiting. All are branches of the oscillation that neither forgiveness nor guidance meets (4:137). For the weak this is a clearing: where you were divided into two groups about the hypocrites (4:88) and told not to take them as allies unless they emigrate (4:89), the painful punishment is the news that the division is not equal — to ally with disbelievers for honour is not the community's way, as the upright way of Abraham (4:125) was never alliance with many.

**Painful Punishment as the Measure of Deception's Pain**

The attribute *alīm* — painful — was explained as the measure where deception sought to avoid pain: the lagger sought to avoid disaster by lagging (4:72); the emigrant sought many havens to escape oppression (4:100); the self-wronger sought advocacy to avoid blame (4:107); hypocrisy seeks to avoid the pain of standing for justice (4:135) by belonging to neither side (4:143). The sūrah says pain is shared — *if you suffer, they suffer* (4:104) — yet the hypocrite who belongs nowhere suffers twice: belonging without hope, and pain without reward. The painful punishment is therefore not arbitrary but the hypocrite's own avoided pain returned as lasting pain — as Hell without escape (4:121) was the delusion's end. The next verses name the seeking that makes it painful — honour sought through wrong company — and the sitting that makes company like them.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:139

> who choose disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour and power through that company? Surely all honour and power belongs to Allah

**Who Choose Disbelievers as Allies Instead of Believers**

The verse states *alladhīna yattakhidhūna al-kāfirīna awliyāʾa min dūni al-muʾminīn* — those who take disbelievers as allies, guardians, protectors, instead of the believers. *Yattakhidhūna awliyāʾ* — to take as allies — was explained with *walī* — guardian, protector, helper — the same *walī* God alone suffices as (4:45), the helper the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75), the Trustee who suffices (4:132). *Min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers — was read as choosing the other company while believers are available, as earlier *do not take them as allies unless they emigrate* (4:89) conditioned alliance on emigration, and as the warning repeated at *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — would you give God proof against yourselves?* (4:144). The sūrah has traced alliances from the lagger who acted as if no bond of affection bound him (4:73), to the double safety-seekers (4:91), to the treaty people excepted (4:90), to Satan taken as guardian instead of Him (4:119); here the allies taken are disbelievers instead of believers — the natural choice of the hypocrites who oscillate (4:137, 4:143), for whom the side promising honour without justice seems attractive.

**Do They Seek Honour and Power Through That Company?**

The question *a-yabtaghūna ʿindahumu al-ʿizzah* — do they seek, pursue, honour, might, power, at their side, through that company? — was explained with *ʿizzah* — honour, might, invincibility. *Abtaghā ʿindahum* — to seek at their side — was read as seeking honour where honour is not: with those who disbelieve, whose schemes are weak (4:76) and whose abode is Hell without escape (4:121), versus Gardens true (4:122). The sūrah has shown that honour was already claimed by those who believed in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* and declared the disbelievers better guided (4:51); to seek *ʿizzah* among disbelievers instead of believers is to repeat that evaluative reversal — to call weakness honour. Early reports linked the verse to hypocrites who cultivated Quraysh connections for protection and status in Madinah while claiming belief; the question exposes the transaction: alliance traded for honour, where alliance for God was available — with the Owner of all (4:131).

**Surely All Honour and Power Belongs to God**

The answer *fa-inna al-ʿizzata li Allāhi jamīʿā* — then surely all, entirely, honour and power belongs to God — was explained with *jamīʿan* — entirely, all together — the same totality as *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth* repeated three times (4:126, 4:131, 4:132), and as *with Him are both rewards* (4:134). *Al-ʿizzah li Allāh* — honour belongs to Him — was read as that honour is not transferred by taking allies; it is His to give to whom He wills — as He took Abraham as close friend (4:125): friendship with the Owner of honour is honour. The sūrah has said God suffices as Guardian and Helper (4:45), suffices as Trustee (4:132), and is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131); to seek honour beside Him is to seek among the encompassed (4:126) from those who own nothing. As all in the heavens and earth belong to Him, all honour belongs to Him — so the seeker who takes disbelievers as allies seeks at the side of those who have no honour to give.

**A Verse That Names the Transaction Behind Oscillation**

Placed after *give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites* (4:138), this verse names the transaction behind oscillation: they believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then increased (4:137), torn between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) — because they sought honour where alliance seemed to supply it. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance and follows other than the believers' path is left to what he chose (4.115) — choosing disbelievers as allies is that following; and that associating is far straying (4:116) — seeking honour among associators is that straying's economy. Where the sūrah says *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves* (4:135), seeking honour from wrong company is the desire that deviates: to witness for disbelievers to gain honour, instead of witnessing for God though against yourselves, is the precise inversion. For the weak this is steadying: honour is not with the company that wishes you to deviate (4:27), nor with Satan's deluding promise (4:120), but with Him whose earth is spacious (4:100) and whose promise is ever true (4:122).

**Honour That Is Entirely His Leaves No Honour With Them**

The word *jamīʿan* — entirely — was explained to leave no remainder with those chosen as allies: if all honour is His, none is at their side to give. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens from Him (4:100), that the doer of good, male or female, enters Paradise not wronged a speck (4.124) because grace is His, and that the best faith is submission to Him (4:125) — friendship with Him is the honour. To choose disbelievers as allies instead of believers is therefore not a neutral social choice but a theological claim — that honour is elsewhere — which the ownership verses deny: *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth* — honour included. The next verse shows the company that seeks such honour in sitting: when you hear the revelations denied or ridiculed, do not sit in that company unless they turn to another topic, else you are like them — and He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:140

> He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah's revelations being denied or ridiculed, then do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic, or else you will be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell

**When You Hear Revelations Denied or Ridiculed — Do Not Sit**

The verse states *wa qad nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi an idhā samiʿtum āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear God's signs being denied or mocked, do not sit with them until they plunge into another discourse. *Qad nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitāb* — He has already revealed to you in the Book — was explained as referencing the earlier command *when you see those who engage in Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in other talk* (6:68) — the principle already revealed, recited again for the hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139). *Āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā* — signs denied or ridiculed — was explained as the denial that makes association far straying (4:116), and the mockery that is the distorter's weapon, as the sūrah has shown that those given a portion distort words and say *we hear and disobey* (4:46), while Satan promises only delusion (4:120). *Fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum* — do not sit with them — was read as a prohibition of company, not merely of speech, matching the rule that no good lies in most secret talks except charity, kindness, and reconciliation (4:114) — sitting where signs are ridiculed is the secret talk without those goods. *Ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — until they plunge into another topic — was read as the limit: withdrawal until the subject changes, not permanent severance from all conversation.

**Or Else You Will Be Like Them**

The consequence *innakum idhan mithluhum* — surely you, then, are like them — was explained as moral assimilation: sitting where signs are denied or mocked, without protest or leaving, makes the sitter like the denier and mocker, even while he claims belief. *Mithluhum* — like them — was read with the sūrah's standard of witness: witnesses for God must stand even against themselves (4:135); to sit silently is the sitter's testimony that the denied sign is not worth standing for. The sūrah has shown that the ally of a treaty people is excepted from hostility (4:90), that the ambiguous community is warned against (4:89), and that advocates for the deceitful are refused (4:105–107); to sit is to advocate by presence. Early notes linked the verse to hypocrites who kept company with Quraysh mockers for honour (4:139): to seek honour among mockers while revelations are ridiculed is to be like the mocker whose company conferred the honour. The phrase was also linked to *whoever distorts testimony or refuses to give it* (4:135) — sitting is refusing testimony where signs need witnesses for Him.

**He Will Gather Hypocrites and Disbelievers Together in Hell**

The gathering *inna Allāha jāmiʿu al-munāfiqīna wa al-kāfirīna fī Jahannama jamīʿā* — surely God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell — was explained with *jāmiʿ* — Gatherer — the same Gatherer who will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87). *Jamīʿan* — all together — was read as that sitting together in mockery in this life ends as being gathered together in Hell: company chosen becomes company assigned. The sūrah has shown that the hypocrite sways between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143), yet the sitter with mockers is counted *like them* (4:140); the gathering makes that likeness abiding, without escape (4:121). The phrase was linked to the two company-endings of the sūrah: Gardens under which rivers flow forever, where God's promise is ever true (4:122), versus Hell as home without escape (4.121): the sitting that was for honour (4:139) ends in gathering for humiliation. For the weak this is the lightest of warnings: to rise from mocking company is not enmity but survival — not sitting is the Book's own instruction.

**A Verse That Follows Honour Sought With Company Prohibited**

Placed after *who choose disbelievers as allies seeking honour — surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139), this verse follows honour sought with company prohibited. The hypocrites sought honour through the company of disbelievers (4:139); the verse says the company where signs are denied or mocked is precisely where you may not sit lest you become like them — so the honour sought there ends as gathered humiliation. The sūrah has shown that trusteeship suffices (4:132), that He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133), and that both rewards are with Him (4:134); to sit with mockers for worldly honour is to desire this world's reward from anyone but Him — where both rewards are with Him. The sūrah has also shown that standing for justice as witnesses for Him, though against yourselves (4:135), requires leaving where justice is mocked; to remain seated where signs are denied is to distort testimony. The verse generalises the sūrah's procedure of verification: verify a report of security or fear through the Messenger and those in authority (4:83); be sure before fighting one who offers peace (4:94); here, where a sitter hears signs denied, verify by leaving — until other talk.

**Gathering Together as the Company's End**

The verb *jāmiʿ* — Gatherer — was explained to show that company is repaid with company: the other world assigns the company chosen in this one. Company where secret talks had no good except charity, kindness, and reconciliation (4:114) belongs to the gathering of believers and doers of good in Gardens (4:122); company where signs are mocked belongs to the gathering of hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell. The sūrah that warned not to be an advocate for the deceitful (4:105) nor for self-wrongers (4:107), and asked *who will be their advocate before God on the Day?* (4:109), here says the advocates of this life who sat with mockers will be gathered with them — not as advocates, but as *like them* (4:140). The next verse shows their waiting: those who wait to see what happens to you, telling each victor *were we not on your side?* (4:141) — waiting is the posture of sitting extended to the battlefield.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:141

> ˹The hypocrites are˺ those who wait to see what happens to you. So if Allah grants you victory, they say ˹to you˺, "Were we not on your side?" But if the disbelievers have a share ˹of victory˺, they say ˹to them˺, "Did we not have the advantage over you, yet we protected you from the believers?" Allah will judge between ˹all of˺ you on the Day of Judgment. And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers

**Those Who Wait and Watch You**

The verse states *alladhīna yatarabbaṣūna bikum* — those who wait, watch, lie in expectation regarding you. *Yatarabbaṣūna* — to wait, watch for the outcome — was explained as the hypocrites' posture, between the community divided into two groups about them (4:88) and the gathering of hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140). To wait regarding you — *bikum* — was read as waiting upon the believers' affairs and battle-turns, as the lagger waited — *he will surely lag behind* — saying on your suffering *God blessed us for not being with them*, and on your gain *would we had been with them* (4:72–73). The waiters here are the same who took disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) and sat where revelations were mocked (4:140); waiting is sitting extended into war: not seated in the mosque where signs are denied, but hovering between armies to see who wins. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens by moving (4:100) and the traveller keeps rank and vigilance in motion (4.101–102); the waiter moves toward neither haven nor rank, but stays to see.

**If You Win, They Claim — Were We Not With You?**

The first face *fa-in kānat lakum fatḥun mina Allāhi qālū a-lam nakun maʿakum* — so if there comes to you a victory, an opening, from God, they say: were we not with you? — was explained with *fatḥ* — victory, opening — as God's opening, the same opening the oppressed invoke — *appoint for us a saviour and helper* (4:75). *A-lam nakun maʿakum* — were we not with you — was read as the claim of belonging after victory: the same claim the lagger makes after gain — *would we had been with them to share the great gain* (4:73) — both seek gain without sharing faith. Early reports noted that such waiters remained in Madinah, not going forth in companies or all together as commanded (4:71), yet claimed a share after. The sūrah has warned *do not take them as allies unless they emigrate* (4:89); the waiter's *were we not with you?* is emigration not done, yet claimed.

**If the Disbelievers Have a Share, They Say — Did We Not Have the Advantage, Yet Protected You?**

The second face *wa-in kāna li-l-kāfirīna naṣībun qālū a-lam nastahwidh ʿalaykum wa namnaʿkum mina al-muʾminīn* — but if the disbelievers have a share of victory, they say to them: did we not have the advantage over you, yet we protected you from the believers? — was explained with *naṣīb* — share, portion — smaller than *fatḥ* — showing that even a partial setback for the believers makes the waiter turn his face. *A-lam nastahwidh ʿalaykum* — did we not gain the upper hand over you — was read as the claim of leverage over the disbelievers: we had power over you; *wa namnaʿkum mina al-muʾminīn* — yet we held the believers back from you — as the claim of protection: by not fighting alongside the believers, by passing information, by saying *we held them off*. The two claims mirror the double-speech of the lagger and the double safety-seekers who wish safety from you and from their own people, yet plunge into *fitnah* whenever they return to it (4:91). The sūrah that warned *Satan promises only delusion* (4:120) here shows the human promisers who promise delivery to both sides.

**God Will Judge Between You on the Day of Resurrection**

The adjudication *fa Allāhu yaḥkumu baynakum yawma al-qiyāmah* — then God will judge, decide, between you all, on the Day of Standing — was explained as the sūrah's promised gathering: He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), after all are gathered on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87), after the souls are taken and asked *what were you doing?* (4:97). *Yaḥkumu baynakum* — will judge between you — was read as between believers, hypocrites, and disbelievers — between the waiter and both winners he courted, between the *fatḥ* claim and the *naṣīb* claim. The sūrah has said the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105), and that He suffices as Trustee (4:132) and Witness (4:79); on the Day the Judge is not eloquence that might sway a human court — where a judge warned that some are more eloquent and could win another's right from him as a piece of fire (al-Bukhārī 2680) — but the All-Knowing who knows what is in hearts (4:63) and who is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108). The judgment separates the waiter's *were we not with you?* from the true with-ness of those with the believers for Gardens (4:122).

**And He Will Never Grant the Disbelievers a Way Over the Believers**

The assurance *wa lan yajʿala Allāhu li-l-kāfirīna ʿalā al-muʾminīna sabīlā* — and God will never grant the disbelievers over the believers a way, a path, an argument — was explained with *sabīl* — way, path, proof, dominance. To grant no *sabīl* for disbelievers over believers was read as the promise that final proof and final dominance belong to faith, not disbelief — as *He will judge between you* ensures the argument is not the waiter's double claim. Early authorities read it both ways — never granting disbelievers a way over believers in proof and victory in this world's end, and the eschatological judgment of the Day; the sūrah holds both: on the Day no *sabīl* remains for disbelief, and in this world, where God wills to make clear and guide to noble ways (4:26), the believer's way is protected where he stands for justice (4:135). The promise was also linked to *all honour belongs to God* (4:139): a way over believers, as a form of honour, is not granted to disbelievers — though a battle's *naṣīb* or *fatḥ* may come and go. For the weak this is steadying: the waiting-between-sides promises no lasting way over you, because He who owns the heavens and earth (4:126) grants none.

**A Verse That Follows Gathering With Waiting and Judgment**

Placed after the gathering of hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), this verse follows gathering with the waiting that made it inevitable, and with the judgment that decides waiting. The hypocrites who believed then disbelieved then increased (4:137), announced as painful punishment (4:138), who chose disbelievers as allies for honour (4:139) and sat where revelations were mocked (4:140), now wait between armies to claim *were we not with you?* to whichever side wins. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here exposes the waiter's desire: to belong without standing — to be ever-standing nowhere, yet claim being-with everywhere. The next verses anatomise that waiting: they seek to deceive God while He outwits them; they stand for prayer lazily, to be seen, remembering little (4:142); swaying between this and that, belonging neither to these nor those — and whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way for him (4:143).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:142

> Surely the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He outwits them. When they stand up for prayer, they do it half-heartedly only to be seen by people—hardly remembering Allah at all

**The Hypocrites Seek to Deceive God — but He Outwits Them**

The verse opens *inna al-munāfiqīna yukhādiʿūna Allāha wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — surely the hypocrites seek to deceive, trick, God, but He outwits them, repaying their deceit. *Yukhādiʿūna* — to seek to deceive, to show other than what is — was explained as hypocrisy's essence: believed then disbelieved then increased (4:137); taking disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139); sitting where revelations are mocked (4:140); waiting between winners to claim *were we not with you?* (4:141). To deceive God was explained as showing belief before the believers while hiding alliance with disbelievers — as plotting by night what displeases Him while He is with them, hiding from people but not from the Encompassing (4:108). *Wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — but He outwits them — was read as recompense: He lets them pursue what they chose (4:115), gathers them with the disbelievers in Hell (4:140), will judge between all on the Day (4:141), and leaves to stray whom He leaves (4:143). The sūrah has said God is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108) and knows what is in hearts (4:63); deception cannot reach Him — it returns upon the deceiver. Early notes linked His outwitting to the divine plan — *they plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters* (3:54): the outwitting is His plan by which the sitting together ends as the gathering together.

**When They Stand for Prayer — Lazily, to Be Seen**

The sign *wa idhā qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti qāmū kusālā yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — and when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, sluggishly, showing off to people — was explained with *qāmū ilā al-ṣalāt* — standing to prayer — the same standing commanded of believers as ever-standing upholders of justice (4:135) and standing for orphans with justice (4:127): here the hypocrites stand to prayer as witnesses not for Him but for people. *Kusālā* — lazy, heavy, sluggish — was explained against the sūrah's vigilance: prayer at its appointed writ (4:103), guarded under arms (4:102), pursuit that does not falter (4:104) — their laziness is the opposite of all vigilance. *Yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — to be seen by people — *riyāʾ* — was read as the same showing off condemned where they spend wealth to be seen of people and believe neither in God nor the Last Day (4:38) — spending to be seen; here standing to be seen. The sūrah has shown there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, and reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114); to stand to be seen is to seek people's pleasure — the honour sought among disbelievers (4:139) — not His.

**Hardly Remembering God at All**

The remainder *wa lā yadhkurūna Allāha illā qalīlā* — and they do not remember God except a little — was explained with *yadhkurūna* — to remember, mention, invoke — the same remembrance commanded standing, sitting, and lying down once prayer is finished (4:103). The sūrah has shown remembrance in all postures as prayer's extension; the hypocrites remember a little — the minimum to be seen, not the remembrance of standing, sitting, lying. *Illā qalīlā* — except a little — was explained as little in quantity and little in sincerity: the few remembrances are themselves for seen-ness. Classical notes added that the little matches the world's little enjoyment (4:77) — hypocrisy trades Gardens forever (4:122) for a little being-seen. The seal contrasts with *whose word is more truthful than God's?* (4:122) and *God is sufficient as Trustee* (4:132): to remember little is to trust little.

**A Verse That Follows Waiting With Deception and Lazy Prayer**

Placed after those who wait and watch, claiming belonging to whichever side wins (4:141), this verse follows waiting with the prayer that reveals waiting's creed: to deceive God, to stand lazily to be seen, to remember little. The sūrah has shown prayer shortened and guarded (4:101–102) and remembered in all postures (4:103) as the believer's discipline that does not falter (4:104); the hypocrite's prayer deforms each — standing yet lazy, present yet for show, remembering but little. The sūrah that commands *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves* (4:135) shows the hypocrite's witness is for people; the sūrah that says *with Him are both rewards; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:134) shows He hears the lazy standing and sees the showing off. The verse was read as the hypocrite's litmus after the announcement of painful punishment (4:138) and the honour sought elsewhere (4:139): the painful punishment is for those whose prayer is for eyes, not for Him.

**Deception Outwitted Becomes Being Gathered Together**

The phrase *He outwits them* was linked to *He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140): the outwitting is the gathering. The hypocrite deceives by sitting where signs are mocked as if not like them — yet the Book says *then you are like them* (4:140); on the Day the likeness becomes the gathering. The sūrah has shown that whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of Him suffers tremendous loss (4:119) and that Satan promises only delusion (4:120); to stand for prayer to be seen is to take people as guardians instead of Him — whose promised honour is delusion. For the weak this is diagnostic: where you stand for prayer after fear, stand vigilant, not lazy; remember much — standing, sitting, lying; seek His pleasure, not people's sight — for He who can remove humanity if He wills (4:133) outwits the deceiver by the very gathering the deceiver thought to avoid by waiting.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:143

> Torn between belief and disbelief—belonging neither to these ˹believers˺ nor those ˹disbelievers˺. And whoever Allah leaves to stray, you will never find for them a way

**Swaying Between — Belonging Neither to These Nor Those**

The verse opens *mudhabdhabīna bayna dhālika lā ilā hāʾulāʾi wa lā ilā hāʾulāʾi* — swaying, wavering, suspended between this and that, belonging neither to these — the believers — nor to those — the disbelievers. *Mudhabdhab* — swayed, shaken, fluttering — was explained as the oscillation already named: believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137); waiting to claim with winners (4:141); deceiving while being outwitted; standing lazily to be seen (4:142). *Bayna dhālika* — between that — was read as between belief and disbelief, between the company with many havens (4:100) and the company without escape (4:121), between Gardens true (4:122) and the Fire prepared. *Neither to these nor to those* was explained as that their alliance with disbelievers instead of believers, sought for honour (4:139), did not make them of the disbelievers; nor did their lazy prayer-to-be-seen (4:142) make them of the believers — they remain between. The sūrah has shown the two companies — hypocrites and disbelievers gathered together in Hell (4:140) versus those who believe and do good in Gardens forever (4:122) — and warned *do not sit with mockers else you are like them* (4:140); the swaying are those who sat, are counted like, yet are not yet fully counted — until the gathering makes the likeness permanent. The image was also linked to the double safety-seekers who wish safety from both sides (4:91), yet belong to neither when *fitnah* returns.

**And Whoever God Leaves to Stray — You Will Never Find a Way for Him**

The seal *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu fa lan tajida lahu sabīlā* — and whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find for him a way — was explained with *yuḍlil* — to leave straying, to not guide — after they turned to what they chose. *Man yuḍlili Allāh* matches *do you wish to guide those God has left to stray?* (4:88) — where the regressed hypocrites were left to regress because of their misdeeds — and *We will let them pursue what they chose* (4:115) after defying the Messenger and following other than the believers' path. *Fa lan tajida lahu sabīlā* — you will never find a way for him — was explained with *sabīl* — way, path, argument, means — the same way God wills to guide to noble ways (4:26), the believers' path not to be left (4:115), and the way He will never grant the disbelievers over the believers (4:141). For the left-to-stray swayers, no way is found: no argument rescues, no sought honour provides a way, no sitting-as-like, no waiting-as-with, no outwitting deception. Early reports pictured the *mudhabdhab* like a sheep between two flocks, or a lost animal between two herders — the image emphasises belonging to none and being found by none.

**A Verse That Follows Lazy Prayer With Wavering Belonging**

Placed after *they seek to deceive God but He outwits them; they stand lazily to be seen, hardly remembering* (4:142), this verse follows lazy prayer with the wavering belonging that lazy prayer manifests. The sūrah has shown prayer as witness for Him even against selves (4:135), remembrance in all postures (4:103), guarded under arms (4:102) — the hypocrite's lazy standing-to-be-seen is witness for people, remembrance little, guard for show; the fruit is being *mudhabdhab* — neither these nor those. The sūrah asked *why are you two groups about the hypocrites?* (4:88); here the hypocrite is himself two parties in one person — neither these nor those. The sūrah that commands mindfulness (4:131), entrusting to Him as Trustee (4:132), believing without wavering (4:136), here says wavering ends with no way found — because the One who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) removes the way from the swaying.

**Left to Stray After Many Clarities**

The phrase *whoever God leaves to stray* was explained as divine leaving after many clarities: association far astray (4:116); the female gods invoked, Satan claimed (4:117–118); the orders to cut and alter (4:119); the promise only delusion (4:120); the two abodes declared true (4:121–122); grace not by wishes (4:123); good with faith not wronged a speck (4:124); best faith as submission following Abraham (4:125); ownership and encompassing (4:126); instruction for orphan women (4:127); settlement best though greed persists (4:128); imperfect emotional justice yet no total inclining (4:129); enrichment after separation (4:130); the universal charge to be mindful (4:131); sufficiency as Trustee (4:132) — after all that, to remain swaying is not ignorance but straying left. The sūrah has said He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, and turn in mercy (4:26–28) — clarity was given; wavering after clarity is the human turning that He lets be. For the weak this is a call to belong: where the next verse says *O believers, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — would you give God proof against yourselves?* (4:144), the wavering between alliances is the proof to abandon — by choosing to be with the believers, for Gardens.

**A Short Verse That Freezes the Hypocrite Between**

Though brief — *swaying between, belonging neither to these nor those; whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way* — the verse freezes the hypocrite between. Immediately after: *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers… would you give God proof against yourselves?* (4:144) — choose a side. Then: *the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire; you will never find for them a helper* (4:145) — except those who repent, mend, hold fast, and are sincere, who will be with the believers, granted a great reward (4:146). The between is therefore not a permanent station; it is a station resolved either into the lowest depth or into being with the believers, according to whether repentance, mending, holding fast, and sincerity replace the swaying. The verse generalises the particular case of waiting between winners (4:141): waiting between is straying left, for whom no way will be found.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:144

> O believers! Do not take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Would you like to give Allah solid proof against yourselves?

**O Believers — Do Not Take Disbelievers as Allies Instead of Believers**

The verse states *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattakhidhū al-kāfirīna awliyāʾa min dūni al-muʾminīn* — O you who believe, do not take disbelievers as allies, guardians, protectors, instead of believers. *Lā tattakhidhū awliyāʾ* — do not take as allies — repeats the description of the hypocrites who chose disbelievers as allies instead of believers, seeking honour (4:139), but now as direct command after the portrait of the swayers, neither these nor those, for whom no way is found (4:143). *Min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers — was explained as choosing the other company while believers are available: as earlier *do not take them as allies unless they emigrate* (4:89) conditioned alliance on emigration, and *those allied to a treaty people are excepted* (4:90) honoured the treaty — but this alliance is taken apart from believers altogether. The sūrah has traced allies from the single soul's family ties (4:1), through dowry and inheritance ties, to the emigrant's haven, to Satan taken as guardian instead of Him — tremendous, manifest loss (4:119); to take disbelievers as guardians instead of believers is to choose the cursed guardian's economy (4:118). Early reports illustrated the command where hypocrites cultivated disbelievers for protection against believers — as if the believers' Trusteeship — *God is sufficient as Trustee* (4:132) — were insufficient; the verse answers: the Trustee suffices, seek no other.

**Would You Give God Clear Proof Against Yourselves?**

The question *a-turīdūna an tajʿalū li Allāhi ʿalaykum sulṭānan mubīnā* — do you want to make for God against you a clear, manifest warrant, proof, authority? — was explained with *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant, manifest proof. The sūrah has already used the phrase the other way: *We have given you clear warrant over such people* — the double-faced who neither withdraw nor offer peace (4:91). Here the warrant is inverted: instead of clear warrant for you against the hostile, you hand God clear warrant against yourselves by allying with disbelievers instead of believers. *To make for God against you* was explained as furnishing the evidence by your own act: to take allies apart from believers while the Book with truth judges between people (4:105) and standing for justice though against yourselves is commanded (4:135) is to write your own indictment. The sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven (4:116) and that the hypocrites and disbelievers will be gathered together in Hell (4:140); to give clear warrant against yourselves is to make that gathering just — because the proof is manifest: honour sought among disbelievers (4:139), sitting where signs are mocked (4:140), waiting to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted (4:142).

**A Verse That Follows the Torn-Between With Choice**

Placed after *swaying between neither these nor those; whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way* (4:143), this verse follows the frozen between with a choice and its evidence. The swaying are told: do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — decide the between. The sūrah has shown that guidance was made clear, noble ways taught, turning offered in mercy (4:26–28), and that He can remove you, O humanity, and bring others (4:133) — removal is the consequence of giving Him clear warrant against yourselves by choosing the other alliance. The sūrah has also shown *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134) — to seek reward from disbeliever allies is to seek little where both are with Him, whose awareness of what you do is exact (4:135, 4:128). The question *do you want?* was read as the Book's appeal to will: do you intend to furnish proof against yourselves — or would you rather stand for justice even against yourselves, and find Him All-Forgiving where you set right and are mindful (4:129)? The choice is not between two honours, but between warrant for you against the hostile (4:91) and warrant for God against you.

**Alliance Instead of Believers Is Itself the Proof**

The phrase *instead of believers* was explained to show that association with disbelievers is not forbidden where treaty or necessity requires dealings — the sūrah excepted those allied to treaty peoples (4:90), allowed setting aside weapons in rain or illness while precaution remains (4:102), and promised many havens among people (4:100). The prohibition is taking them as *awliyāʾ* — intimate guardians — instead of believers: as the oppressed cry for a guardian and helper from grace (4:75), the guardian is to be from Him. Early notes added that the clear warrant against yourselves is not metaphor but record: night plotting with them while He is with you (4:108), advocating for self-wrongers among them (4:107), hiding from people but not from the Encompassing (4:108) — all will be brought as witness. Where the emigrant's reward falls upon God, secure (4:100), the ally-taker's proof falls against himself, secure — because the Trustee who suffices (4:132) keeps a record that encompasses everything (4:126).

**A Short Verse That Anchors Proof in Alliance**

Though brief — *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers; would you give God clear proof against yourselves?* — the verse anchors proof in alliance. Immediately after: *the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire; you will never find for them a helper* (4:145) — except those who repent, mend, hold fast, and are sincere, who will be with the believers, granted a great reward (4:146): the proof either stands or is erased by repentance and holding fast. The sūrah that warns not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) names this alliance as the desire that deviates: to seek protection or honour from those who disbelieve is to swerve from ever-standing justice. For the weak this is the lightest protection: where you feared ill-conduct or turning away in the household, you were given settlement as best (4:128); here, where you might fear and so ally with disbelievers for honour, the lightest is to belong with believers — whose path is submission following Abraham, best faith (4:125), whose Friend is the Owner of the heavens and earth — and not to hand against yourselves the manifest proof whose end is being gathered together in Hell.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:145

> Surely the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire—and you will never find for them any helper—

**The Hypocrites Will Be in the Lowest Depths of the Fire**

The verse states *inna al-munāfiqīna fī al-darki al-asfali mina al-nār* — surely the hypocrites are in the lowest depth, the bottommost level, of the Fire. *Dark* — depth, level, story — *asfal* — lowest — was explained as the deepest layer of Hell — beneath the disbelievers gathered together with the hypocrites (4:140), beneath the self-wronger's Hell as home (4:97), beneath the defier's burning (4:115), beneath the Satan-follower's Hell without escape (4:121). *Of the Fire* was read as the Fire whose preparation was humiliating punishment for the disbelievers behind the guarded prayer (4:102), whose truth is contrasted with the true promise of Gardens (4:122). Its lowest depth is for those who deceive God while He outwits them, stand lazily to be seen (4:142), sway between neither these nor those (4:143), and take disbelievers as allies, giving God clear warrant against themselves (4:144). Early reports noted that the Fire has levels — as Paradise has elevated ranks (4:96) — and the lowest level is assigned to hypocrisy because hypocrisy is the lowest form of deceit: invoking female gods and Satan (4:117) is at least open; to deceive while claiming belief is hidden, and therefore lower. The sūrah has shown that the sitter where signs are mocked is like them (4:140); the lowest depth is the belonging of the swayers who belonged to none.

**And You Will Never Find for Them Any Helper**

The clause *wa lan tajida lahum naṣīrā* — and you will never find for them any helper, supporter — was explained with *naṣīr* — the same helper the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45). To find no helper for the hypocrites was read as that no guardian and no helper remains where they gave Him clear proof against themselves (4:144) and where *whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way* (4:143). *Lan tajida* — you will never find — was addressed to the Prophet ﷺ and to every searcher: no helper will be found for them, as this life's advocates for the deceitful found no advocate or trustee before God on the Day (4:109). The lowest depth without helper contrasts with the Gardens promised to those who believe and do good — rivers flowing, promise true (4:122) — and with enrichment from His bounty for those who part (4:130). Where the emigrant finds many havens and many refuges (4:100), the hypocrite finds the lowest Fire and no helper — because the heavens and earth belong to the One they tried to deceive while He was with them in their night plotting (4:108).

**A Verse That Follows Clear Warrant Against Selves With Depth Without Helper**

Placed after *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?* (4:144), this verse follows the warning with the consequence that manifest proof earns: the lowest depth, no helper. The sūrah has built hypocrisy's proof step by step: oscillation (4:137); painful punishment announced (4:138); honour sought among disbelievers (4:139); sitting where signs are mocked, becoming like them (4:140); waiting to claim with winners (4:141); deceiving, lazy prayer, little remembrance (4:142); swaying between (4:143); allies instead of believers (4:144) — the lowest depth is the depth of that accumulation, as the Gardens' elevated ranks (4:96) are the height of accumulated good, where charity, kindness, and reconciliation were commanded (4:114) and prayer guarded and remembered (4:102–103). Where the sūrah says *do not let desires deviate you from justice; if you distort or refuse, He is All-Aware* (4:135), hypocrisy deviates maximally — twisting testimony and refusing it — so the depth is maximal, and the helper none.

**The Lowest Depth as the Counter to Elevated Ranks**

The *lowest depth* was read as the counter-pole to *ranks from Him* (4:96), where strivers are elevated above sitters though both are promised good. The sūrah has degrees of ascent for strivers — forgiveness, mercy, ranks — and degrees of descent implied here for hypocrites; the lowest depth stands opposite the elevated ranks, as Hell without escape (4:121) stands opposite Gardens forever. The sūrah that says *with Him are both rewards; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:134) says the depth is neither unheard nor unseen: the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Fully Aware (4:126) measures without wronging an atom (4:40) — and the depth for hypocrisy is atom-exact, after many clarities rejected. For the weak this is clarifying: to sway between (4:143) and to ally with disbelievers (4:144) is not a safe middle — it is the lowest; to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is to be with the believers — whose company the next verse makes reachable by repentance, mending, holding fast, and sincerity.

**A Short Verse That Holds the Gate Open One More Verse**

Though brief — *the hypocrites in the lowest depths of the Fire; you will never find for them a helper* — the verse holds the gate open one more verse: the sūrah's own continuation — *except those who repent, mend, hold fast to God, and are sincere* — will return them to being with the believers, granted a great reward (4:146). The sūrah has shown that whoever commits evil then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110), that seeking forgiveness is commanded between the prohibitions on advocacy (4:106), and that whoever earns sin bears it upon himself yet may seek and find (4:111) — the depth without helper is the wage where none of those is done. The mercy that is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving (4:99) is not cancelled by the depth — *except* — so that the lowest depth is not a fate sealed by lineage but by persisting in swaying and alliance; and the gate is sincerity after repentance.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:146

> except those who repent, mend their ways, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their devotion to Allah; they will be with the believers. And Allah will grant the believers a great reward

**Except Those Who Repent, Mend, Hold Fast, and Are Sincere**

The verse states *illā alladhīna tābū wa aṣlaḥū wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāhi wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāh* — except those who repent, turn back, and mend, set right, and hold fast, cling, to God, and make their religion, devotion, sincere, pure for Him. *Tābū* — to repent, return — was explained with the sūrah's *tawbah*: the return soon after error (4:17), before death's *now I repent* (4:18), after deceit and wronging — *whoever wrongs himself then seeks, finds Him All-Forgiving* (4:110). *Wa aṣlaḥū* — and mended — was explained as repairing what was corrupted: where night plotting disordered (4:108), where throwing sin on the innocent burdened (4:112), where honour was sought among disbelievers (4:139), where sitting with mockers made one like them (4:140) — mending is the same *iṣlāḥ* as the reconciliation between people commanded in good counsel (4:114). *Wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāh* — and held fast to God — was explained as the same *iʿtiṣām* by which whoever holds fast to Him is admitted into mercy and guided to a Straight Path (4:175), and by which the emigrant's reward falls secure (4:100). *Wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāh* — and made their devotion sincere for Him — was read as *ikhlāṣ* — purity from showing off — the direct reversal of standing lazily to be seen (4:142) and spending to be seen (4:38); sincerity is the opposite of *riyāʾ* and of seeking honour among disbelievers (4:139). The four verbs were explained as the hypocrite's reversal, stepwise: repentance reverses the oscillation (4:137); mending reverses the plotting and harm; holding fast reverses the alliance instead of believers (4:144); sincerity reverses the standing to be seen.

**They Will Be With the Believers**

The promise *fa ulāʾika maʿa al-muʾminīn* — then those — the repentant, mended, holding, sincere — will be with the believers — was explained with *maʿa* — with — the very word the waiters claimed falsely — *were we not with you?* (4:141) — now made true. To be *with the believers* was read as not merely spared from the lowest depth (4:145) but transferred to the other company: where hypocrites and disbelievers are gathered together in Hell (4:140), the repentant are gathered with the honoured company — the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous (4:69). The sūrah has shown that whoever obeys God and the Messenger will be with those blessed (4:69), and that whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than the believers' path is left to that path (4:115); those who repent and are sincere are returned to the believers' path — after swaying between neither (4:143). The phrase was linked to *Gardens under which rivers flow forever; God's promise is ever true* (4:122): to be with the believers is to share that promise, whose word none exceeds.

**And God Will Grant the Believers a Great Reward**

The seal *wa sawfa yuʾtī Allāhu al-muʾminīna ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and God will grant the believers a great, mighty reward — was explained with *sawfa* — will, soon — certainty, as the emigrant's reward is secured upon God (4:100); and *ajr ʿaẓīm* — great reward — the same reward promised to those who counsel charity, kindness, and reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114), and to strivers above sitters (4:95–96). To promise the great reward now inclusive of the repentant sincere was read as that their repentance does not make them second-class believers — mercy makes them believers. The sūrah has said *whoever commits evil will be recompensed accordingly* (4:123), yet *whoever does good, male or female, with faith will enter Paradise, not wronged a speck* (4:124); the sincere repentant's good is now counted among that good. Where the hypocrites sought honour among disbelievers — though all honour belongs to God (4:139) — the great reward is the honour given to believers, not sought beside Him, because with Him are both rewards (4:134).

**A Verse That Follows the Lowest Depth With the Highest Return**

Placed after *the hypocrites in the lowest depths of the Fire; you will never find for them a helper* (4:145), this verse follows the lowest with the return. The sūrah announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138) and traced their portrait — honour sought wrongly, sitting where mocked, waiting between, deceiving, lazy prayer, swaying, alliance giving clear proof against selves (4:138–144); here the same hypocrites are given four steps: repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere. The sūrah will ask *why should God punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing* (4:147) — punishment is not needed where gratitude and faith are; these four are that gratitude and faith made operational. The sūrah that asked *was God's earth not spacious enough for you to emigrate?* (4:97) and promised many havens (4:100) here says the earth's spaciousness includes a haven from the lowest depth to being with the believers — via sincerity. For the weak the sūrah lightens: where standing for justice though against yourselves was hard (4:135), holding fast to God is the stand; where settlement is best (4:128), mending is the settlement made with Him; where greed was present (4:128), sincerity removes it.

**Four Verbs That Reverse Four Hypocrisies**

The four — *tābū, aṣlaḥū, iʿtaṣamū, akhlaṣū* — were read as a stepwise remedy for the hypocrite's defects: *tābū* heals the oscillation that left belief (4:137); *aṣlaḥū* heals the counsel without good — the night plot and the slander (4:114, 4:108); *iʿtaṣamū* heals the alliance taken instead of believers (4:144), restoring trust to the Trustee who suffices (4:132); *akhlaṣū* heals the showing off where prayer was for people (4:142). The verse generalises the judgment chapter's medicine — *whoever wrongs himself then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving* (4:110): seeking is repentance; mending is setting right; holding fast is reliance on the sufficient Trustee; sincerity is doing for Him, not for eyes. The next verse states the principle that makes these four sufficient: *why should God punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing* (4:147) — so that those with Him are promised great reward not out of His need, but out of His appreciation.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:147

> Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and faithful? Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing

**Why Should God Punish You If You Are Grateful and Faithful?**

The verse opens *mā yafʿalu Allāhu bi-ʿadhābikum in shakartum wa āmantum* — what would God do with your punishment — why should He punish you — if you are grateful and believe. *What would He do with your punishment* was explained as rhetorical negation: He has no need to punish, as He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) — to Him still belongs all though you disobey — and He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133). *If you are grateful and believe* was read with *shukr* — gratitude — and *īmān* — faith — the two that give the four of the previous verse their life: repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere (4:146) — the gratitude and faith that replace swaying between (4:143) and alliances instead of believers (4:144). *Shakartum* was explained as gratitude shown in act: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114); doing good, male or female, with faith (4:124); submitting the face and doing good, following Abraham (4:125); standing for justice (4:135); holding fast to Him (4:175). *Wa āmantum* — and believe — was explained as comprehensive faith in God, His Messenger, the Books, the angels, the Last Day (4:136), renewed without wavering — steadfast, versus the oscillation that only increased (4:137). Early reports linked the verse to the repentant hypocrites just promised being with the believers and a great reward (4:146): why should He punish, if they are now grateful and faithful? The sūrah has shown that whoever seeks forgiveness after evil finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110), and that He forgives what is less than association for whom He wills (4:116); gratitude and faith are that seeking made character.

**Allah Is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Shākiran ʿAlīmā* — and God is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing — was explained with *Shākir* — Appreciative, Rewarding of thanks — the One who appreciates the grateful and repays gratitude with increase, as *if you are grateful, I will surely increase you* (14:7). *Shākir* was read as that He rewards the thankful with the great reward just promised (4:146) and the great favour already shown (4:113). *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — was explained as knowing gratitude and faith even where hidden, as He is Fully Aware, encompassing everything (4:126), All-Aware of what you do (4:128, 4:135), All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) — nothing of gratitude or faith escapes Him. The pairing *Shākir ʿAlīm* fits the context where thanks is repaid: He knows the gratitude, and He appreciates it. The sūrah has sealed acts with knowledge names throughout — All-Knowing, All-Wise where sin is earned (4:111); *Muḥīṭ* where night plotting hid (4:108); here *Appreciative, All-Knowing* seals grateful faith as the act He rewards.

**A Verse That Follows Repentance With Principle**

Placed after *except those who repent, mend, hold fast, and are sincere — they will be with the believers, granted a great reward* (4:146), this verse follows repentance with the principle that explains why repentance works: why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? The sūrah has announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138) and the lowest depth without helper (4:145) — yet opened the exception; the principle answers the implied question: does He punish because He needs to? — *what would He do with your punishment* — He has no need, being Self-Sufficient (4:131) and sufficient as Trustee (4.132). Where He can remove and bring others (4:133), He does not need to keep punishing; where both rewards are with Him (4:134), He needs not withhold. The principle therefore transforms threat into invitation: the same God who declared grace is not by wishes (4:123) and evil is recompensed accordingly (4:123) says His punishment is not sought for itself; gratitude and faith remove its cause — and being Appreciative, He rewards them. The sūrah's ethic — stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), have faith entire (4:136) — is therefore not burden but gratitude that He appreciates.

**Grateful and Faithful as the Antidote to Hypocrisy**

The pair *grateful and faithful* was explained as the antidote to hypocrisy's pair — deceiving and showing off (4:142): gratitude is sincerity in devotion where showing off was; faith is holding fast where the alliance instead of believers was. The sūrah has shown that Satan promises only delusion (4:120) — gratitude for the true promise (4:122) counters delusion; that no good lies in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — grateful action commands those three. The verse was linked to *if you are grateful, I will increase you; but if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe* (14:7): gratitude increases the good, while ingratitude resembles the increase in disbelief (4:137). The seal *Appreciative, All-Knowing* therefore says: He who commanded returning trusts (4:58) will repay trust kept; He who knows what is in hearts (4:63) knows whether gratitude stood where greed pressed (4:128) and whether faith held where desire pulled (4:135).

**A Short Verse That Holds Needlessness and Appreciation Together**

Though brief — *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing* — the verse holds needlessness and appreciation together. The chapter that began *be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul* (4:1), showed ownership of the heavens and earth, sufficiency as Trustee, and capability to replace (4:126–133), warned against allies instead of believers lest you give clear proof against yourselves (4:144), declared the lowest depth without helper (4:145), yet opened the *except* of four — now says punishment itself is not His need: gratitude and faith are what He appreciates and knows. For the weak this is the lightest of principles: where you feared ill-conduct and settlement is best (4:128), to be grateful where settlement waives, and faithful where trust is held, is not heavy — because the Appreciative knows it, and will not punish where it is. The next passage turns from principle to the law of speech: God does not like the open voicing of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged — He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing (4:148).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:148

> Allah does not like negative thoughts to be voiced—except by those who have been wronged. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing

**God Does Not Like Evil Speech Voiced Openly — Except by the Wronged**

The verse states *lā yuḥibbu Allāhu al-jahra bi-al-sūʾi mina al-qawli illā man ẓulim* — God does not like, love, the loud voicing — *jahr* — of evil, bad speech, except by one who has been wronged, oppressed. *Al-jahra bi-al-sūʾi min al-qawl* — to voice evil openly, to proclaim bad speech aloud — was explained as public complaint, accusation, vile talk — as the sūrah has shown that those who hide from people while God is with them, where they plot displeasing speech (4:108), own precisely that evil speech He dislikes; and that the advocates who dispute on behalf of the deceitful in this life use loud evil speech (4:107–109). *Lā yuḥibbu* — does not like — parallels *God does not like the deceitful sinner* (4:107) and *God does not like the stingy who promote stinginess* (4:37): to voice evil openly is disliked as greed and treachery are. *Illā man ẓulim* — except by the wronged — was explained as permission for the oppressed — the same weak who cry *deliver us from this land of oppressors; appoint for us a saviour and helper* (4:75) — to voice their wrong: to complain of oppression, to seek redress, to report injustice.
