The phrase *though they were forbidden it* was explained as breaking after knowledge — after compelling proof (4:153), after the Mount raised, after the firm covenant with the Sabbath's limit (4:154): the prohibition of ribā is of that rank. Taking despite prohibition continues the litany: demand, thunderbolt, calf, breaking, rejecting, killing, sealed hearts, denial, slander, boast — now forbidden foods for wrongdoing and hindering — now ribā despite prohibition and wealth consumed unjustly. The pattern is breaking after being shown, as *those who believed then disbelieved then increased* (4:137): increase after clarity. The sūrah that allows no good counsel except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) here unmasks ribā as counsel's devouring counterfeit.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Wealth in Disbelief Among Them**

Though brief — *taking interest despite its prohibition, and consuming people's wealth unjustly — We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment* — the verse anchors the punishment in the disbelievers among them, not in all. The exception appears next: *but those of them well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful who believe in what was revealed to you and before you — especially those who establish prayer and those who pay alms and believe in God and the Last Day — to them We will grant a great reward* (4:162). Elsewhere the promise says *whoever does good, male or female, with faith will enter Paradise, not wronged a speck* (4:124), and both rewards are with Him (4:134): to pay alms is the opposite of taking ribā — releasing wealth where ribā extracts it. The next verse shows the forbidding of pure foods is not permanence: for the grounded faithful, the reward is great — with the pure restored in Gardens where the promise is true.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:162

> But those of them well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful ˹who˺ believe in what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what was revealed before you—˹especially˺ those who establish prayer—and those who pay alms-tax and believe in Allah and the Last Day, to these ˹people˺ We will grant a great reward

**But Those of Them Well-Grounded in Knowledge**

The verse states *lākini ar-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilmi minhum* — but those firmly grounded, deeply rooted, in knowledge, among them. *Rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm* — firmly grounded in knowledge — was explained as those rooted so deep that no wind moves them — the opposite of those who desire a way between God and His messengers (4:150) — as Abraham was upright, *ḥanīf* (4:125), and as the Book was sent with truth to judge by what He shows (4:105). *Among them* was read with the sūrah's balance: as painful punishment was prepared for the *disbelievers among them* (4:161), so the great reward is for the *grounded among them* — they believe except for a few (4:155) — here the few are named. The verse answers the accusation that the Qur'an condemns a whole people: it distinguishes within them, as it distinguished the helpless (4:98) and the repentant (4:146) elsewhere. Early reports and commentators counted among the *rāsikhūn* of the earlier communities figures like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions — those of the People of the Book who recognised the Prophet ﷺ as they recognised their own sons.

**The Faithful Who Believe in What Was Revealed to You and Before You**

The description *wa al-muʾminūna yuʾminūna bi-mā unzila ilayka wa mā unzila min qablika* — and the believers who believe in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you — was explained as comprehensive faith that makes no distinction between any messenger (4:152) and accepts the whole lineage: revelation sent as to Noah and the prophets after him — Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, and the Psalms to David (4:163). To believe in what was sent down to you *and* what was sent down before you was read as the faith commanded: *have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — steadfast, not selective; the grounded are those who kept it. The sūrah has shown that *whoever believes in God and His messengers, making no distinction among any of them — He will give them their rewards* (4:152): these are they.

**Especially Those Who Establish Prayer and Pay Alms**

The detail *wa al-muqīmīna aṣ-ṣalāta wa al-muʾtūna az-zakāta* — and especially those who establish prayer, and those who give the purifying alms — was explained with two pillars. *Establishing prayer* is the same prayer commanded at its fixed writ (4:103), shortened on travel (4:101), guarded under arms (4:102), remembered standing, sitting, and lying (4:103) — which the hypocrites stood for lazily to be seen (4:142); the grounded establish it. *Paying alms* was read as the opposite of taking interest and consuming wealth unjustly (4.161): to give *zakāh* is to release wealth; to take ribā is to extract it. Early reports noted the grammar — the accusative *al-muqīmīna* reads as special praise, as Arabic singles out the praised — showing the emphasis on those who establish prayer among the grounded. The pair was also linked to *Gardens for those who believe and do good* (4:122): establishing prayer and giving alms are the righteous deeds.

**And Those Who Believe in God and the Last Day — To Them a Great Reward**

The seal *wa al-muʾminīna bi Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri ulāʾika sa-nuʾtīhim ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and those who believe in God and the Last Day — to these We will surely grant a great, mighty reward — was explained with belief in God and the Last Day as the two articles that anchor all: to deny God, the angels, the Books, the messengers, or the Last Day is to go far astray (4:136); the grounded affirm them. *A great reward* is the same *ajr ʿaẓīm* promised for counselling charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), for the repentant sincere with the believers (4:146), and for the comprehensive believers (4:152) — the grounded who establish prayer and give alms are included among them. The sūrah has shown *with Him are both rewards; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:134): the great reward is both worlds. *We will surely grant* was read as divine assurance, as the emigrant's reward is secured upon God (4:100).

**A Verse That Follows Disbelief Among Them With Faith Among Them**

Placed after forbidden foods for wrongdoing and hindering (4:160) and ribā with unjust consumption for the disbelievers among them (4:161), this verse follows disbelief among them with faith among them: but the well-grounded in knowledge among them, the faithful who believe in what was revealed to you and before you, establishing prayer, paying alms, believing in God and the Last Day — to them a great reward. The sūrah has shown that even after the whole litany — demand, thunderbolt, calf, breaking, rejecting, killing, sealed hearts, slander, boast — there remain the grounded, who make no distinction among messengers (4:152) and receive the great reward. The verse was read as the sūrah's middle between condemnation and hope, after the ownership of the heavens and earth (4:126) — the grounded accept that ownership and the witness borne with His knowledge (4:166). For the weak this is opening: where interest was extracted and wealth consumed unjustly, the grounded who give alms enrich without stripping, as the separated were enriched from His bounty (4.130) — the great reward includes the pure things restored.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:163

> Indeed, We have sent revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ as We sent revelation to Noah and the prophets after him. We also sent revelation to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants, ˹as well as˺ Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon. And to David We gave the Psalms

**We Have Sent Revelation to You as We Sent It to Noah and Those After Him**

The verse opens *innā awḥaynā ilayka kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin wa an-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — indeed We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. *We revealed* — *awḥaynā* — was explained as divine communication into the heart, the sending of the Book with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105), and the faith commanded: *have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — revelation is one chain. *As We revealed to Noah* was read as Noah being the first of the chain of messengers to nations after Adam — his ark upon water that belongs to Him (4:126) being the first rescue of the single soul's spread (4:1). *And the prophets after him* was explained as that the revelation to you is not isolated but continuation — as Abraham was upright and taken as friend (4.125) and his way is the best faith. The verse generalises the sūrah's lineage: from Noah through Abraham to you is one revelation, whose truth was witnessed where the Mount was raised (4:154) and whose non-distinction is true belief (4:152).

**Also to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes**

The enumeration begins *wa awḥaynā ilā Ibrāhīma wa Ismāʿīla wa Isḥāqa wa Yaʿqūba wa al-asbāṭ* — and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes, his descendants. Abraham's line was read as the upright Way of Abraham (4:125) made concrete: revelation came to each branch — not only to the People of the Book who demanded a book from heaven (4.153); the book had already come to many. Ishmael was read as the line of the Arabs — the Prophet's ﷺ forefather — placed beside Isaac, so that neither descent line claims revelation exclusively. Jacob and the tribes — *al-asbāṭ*, his twelve sons — were read as the whole people of Israel covered: their revelation was one chain from their father. The enumeration thus makes *believing in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you* (4:162) a concrete list, not an abstraction.

**Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon — and the Psalms to David**

The enumeration continues *wa ʿĪsā wa Ayyūba wa Yūnusa wa Hārūna wa Sulaymāna wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon; and to David We gave the Psalms. Jesus was read as the Messiah raised to Himself (4:158), son of the Mary slandered, whose killing was boasted though never done — now placed among the prophets revealed to, not a god — so that honouring him needs no extremity (4:171). Job and Jonah were read as the tested: Job in patient affliction, Jonah in repentance after leaving — revelation includes trials. Aaron and Solomon were read as brother-helper and king-prophet: Aaron beside Moses where the Mount was raised (4:154), Solomon with a kingdom that could not withhold a speck (4:53) — even kingdom accompanied prophethood. *To David We gave the Psalms* — *Zabūr* — was explained as a Book singled out among the Scriptures before (4:136): Books before are many, not the single book from heaven demanded (4:153). The likeness *as We revealed* is in source — all from the Owner of the heavens and earth (4:126) — and in purpose — to judge and make clear with truth.

**A Verse That Follows the Demand for a Book With the Lineage of Revelation**

Placed after the whole history of demand and correction (4:153–162), this verse follows the demand for a book from heaven with the lineage: We have sent revelation to you as We sent it to Noah and the prophets after him. The demand (4:153) is answered: revelation has already come to many, including the Psalms to David — the demand is not for the first book but for a spectacle. The sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers desire a way between (4:150) — to distinguish is to claim the lineage broken; this verse says the lineage is one. The sūrah that will warn not to go to extremes in religion — the Messiah was only a messenger, God's Word through Mary and a spirit from Him (4:171) — here places Jesus among the prophets revealed to, so that extremity is unnecessary to honour him.

**Revelation to Many Makes Faith Without Distinction Possible**

The phrase *as We revealed* was explained to make *accepting all, rejecting none* (4:152) possible: because the source is one — the Owner of the heavens and earth (4:126) — to accept all is to accept that Owner's many gifts. Where the hypocrites sway between neither these nor those (4:143) and desire a way between by distinguishing (4:150), the lineage from Noah to David to you is the firm path — the believers' path (4:115) — not wavering. For the weak this is an opening: where settlement is best (4:128) and settlement involves waiving a right, the lineage of revelation shows no waiving of any prophet; faith is not a settlement that waives some messengers, but upright submission that accepts all. The next verse extends the lineage: messengers whose stories We told you and others We did not, and to Moses God spoke directly (4:164).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:164

> There are messengers whose stories We have told you already and others We have not. And to Moses Allah spoke directly

**Messengers Whose Stories We Told You, and Others We Did Not**

The verse states *wa rusulan qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣ-hum ʿalayka* — and messengers whose stories We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you. *Messengers* continues the lineage just named — Noah and the prophets after him, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, and David given the Psalms (4:163). *Whose stories We have related to you before* was read as those named through the Qur'an — told as proof that God bears witness with His knowledge (4:166). *And messengers We have not related to you* was explained as that knowledge belongs to Him who is Fully Aware, encompassing everything (4:126): He sent many more than were told — among all peoples, as elsewhere *every nation had a warner* (35:24). The sūrah has shown that the grounded believe in what was revealed to you *and* what was revealed before you (4.162) — the messengers not recounted are included in that belief, for their existence is asserted here. To be told that some were not told was explained as humility of the Book: it does not claim to list all whom He sent, because the heavens and earth belong to Him (4:126) — He sent and He knows. The charge to be mindful (4:131) therefore rests not on counting messengers but on trusting the Sender, whose knowledge encompasses the unnamed as *Muḥīṭ*.

**And to Moses God Spoke Directly**

The addition *wa kallama Allāhu Mūsā taklīmā* — and God spoke to Moses with direct speech — was explained with *taklīm* — speaking directly, without intermediary — the honour by which Moses is called *Kalīmullāh*, the one addressed by God. *Taklīmā* — the emphatic verbal noun — was read as absolute direct speech, distinct from the inspiration given to Noah and the prophets (4:163). Early reports linked this to Sinai, where the Mount was raised for the covenant (4:154) and the thunderbolt struck the demand to see God visibly (4:153) — yet to Moses He spoke directly, without Moses seeing Him. The sūrah has shown that the crucifixion boast had *no knowledge, only assumption* (4:157): true knowledge is where He speaks, as He spoke to Moses. The verse also answers the People of the Book's demand to *bring down a book from heaven* (4:153): revelation has already been spoken — directly — to a messenger of their own line.

**A Verse That Follows the Lineage With the Limit of Narration**

Placed after the full lineage — Noah through the prophets to David's Psalms (4:163) — this verse follows lineage with the limit of narration: some related, some not related, and Moses spoken to directly. The sūrah has commanded those before you and you to be mindful (4:131) — revelation before you is many; that some are not narrated does not deny them, for He hears and sees (4:134) and knows those sent. The sūrah that warns not to make distinction between messengers (4:150–152) includes the unnamed in that non-distinction: accepting all messengers includes those whose names were not given. And the sūrah that warns against allies instead of believers (4:144) makes the direct speech to Moses a help for the weak: where disputes are referred to God and the Messenger (4:59), here is the Speaker who can be referred to.

**Direct Speech as Proof After the Demand for the Visible**

The phrase *God spoke to Moses directly* was linked to the initial demand — *bring down a book from heaven* — and its predecessor — *show us God plainly* (4:153): Moses heard Him directly, yet his people still demanded the visible, took the calf after clear signs, and broke the covenant, so the Mount was raised (4:154). Direct speech did not suffice for those demanding the visible; to demand the visible after speech is the wrongdoing for which pure foods were forbidden (4:160). For the community, direct speech is the proof that the Book was sent with truth — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105): He shows by speaking clearly.

**The Unrecounted Messengers and Comprehensive Faith**

The mention of messengers not narrated was explained to include distant peoples and times: revelation untold is still revelation to be believed, as faith guards — *have faith in God, His Messenger, the Books, the angels, the Last Day* (4:136) — and not to know a messenger's name does not remove the command to accept all (4:152). The sūrah has shown that even an error before prayer is covered by pardon where sincerity is sought (4:43): unknowing is treated differently from defying after clarity (4:115). The next verse names the purpose of all messengers, narrated or not: bearers of good news and warners, so that humanity has no excuse before God after the messengers — and He is Almighty, All-Wise (4:165).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:165

> ˹All were˺ messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity should have no excuse before Allah after ˹the coming of˺ the messengers. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise

**Messengers as Bearers of Good News and Warners**

The verse states *rusulan mubashshirīna wa mundhirīn* — messengers as bearers of good news and warners. The two faces of their message were explained as already named in the sūrah: Gardens forever under which rivers flow, where God's promise is ever true (4:122) — the good news; and Hell without escape for the followers of Satan's delusion (4:121), painful punishment for the hypocrites (4:138), humiliating punishment for the true disbelievers who distinguish (4:151), and painful punishment for the disbelievers among the People of the Book for wrongdoing, ribā, and unjust consumption (4:161) — the warnings. *Messengers* includes those whose stories were told and those not narrated, and Moses spoken to directly (4:164), and David given the Psalms (4:163), and the chain from Noah through Abraham to Jesus (4:163) — all bore good news and warning. The sūrah has shown that those who believe, accepting all and rejecting none, will be given their rewards (4:152), and the grounded believe in what was sent to you and before you (4:162) — the good news is theirs; and *whoever commits evil will be recompensed with it, finding no protector besides God* (4:123) — the warning is his.

**So That Humanity Has No Excuse Before God After the Messengers**

The purpose *li-allā yakūna li-an-nāsi ʿalā Allāhi ḥujjatun baʿda ar-rusul* — so that humanity may have no argument, excuse, plea, against God after the messengers — was explained with *ḥujjah* — argument — the same word as the clear warrant given over the double-faced (4:91), the warrant warned against giving against yourselves (4:144), and the compelling proof Moses was given (4:153): after the messengers, humanity's argument against Him is removed. *After the messengers* was read as after the lineage from Noah to the final messenger — no *we did not know* remains, because He who could remove humanity and bring others (4:133) sent messengers first. Early reports linked this to the sūrah's will to make clear, guide to noble ways, and turn in mercy (4:26): clarity comes by messengers, so the excuse is cut. The phrase was linked to the Messiah as witness against them on the Day (4:159) and the witness from every community and the Prophet ﷺ against his (4:41) — witnesses are messengers, and the witness is the argument. Where the hypocrites sought to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142) and argued *we believe in some and disbelieve in some* (4:150) — claiming an argument of compromise — the verse says none remains.

**And God Is Almighty, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīmā* — and God is ever Almighty, All-Wise — was explained with *ʿAzīz* — Almighty — the One who raised Jesus to Himself (4:158) and can remove humanity (4:133), yet sends warners before any removal; and *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — who sends good news and warning in wisdom, not need. The pair seals the sending as strong: the good news and the warning are backed by an Almighty who can do as He warns, and a Wise who warns where warning is wise — as He is Most Capable to pardon though capable to punish (4:149) and All-Forgiving, Most Merciful in rewarding: good news is mercy from the Wise; warning is justice from the Mighty. The sūrah has shown He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy though you disobey (4:131) — He needs no argument from you; He removes yours.

**A Verse That Follows the Lineage With Purpose**

Placed after the lineage of revelation (4:163) and the told and untold messengers with Moses' direct speech (4:164), this verse follows lineage with purpose: all were bearers of good news and warnings, so that humanity has no excuse after the messengers — and He is Almighty, All-Wise. The sūrah has traced the demand for a book from heaven, the greater demand for visible God, the thunderbolt, the calf, the covenant and its breaking, the slander and the boast, the raising, the forbidding of pure foods, ribā, unjust consumption, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, and a great reward for the grounded (4:153–162) — now the *why* of all that sending: so that no excuse remains. The sūrah that asked *was God's earth not spacious enough for you to emigrate?* (4:97) and promised many havens (4:100) says: the messengers are the spaciousness of excuse removed, as the earth is the spaciousness of refuge opened. For the weak this is clarifying: where settlement is best (4:128), the good news is that pleasing settlement earns great reward (4:114); the warning is that total inclining leaves a hanging — both were told before the excuse remained.

**The Excuse Removed Is the Hypocrite's Argument**

The argument removed — *no excuse against God after the messengers* — was linked to *would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?* (4:144): the warrant hypocrites hand over by allying with disbelievers for honour (4:139) is the excuse that remains against them. The messengers sent as bearers of good news and warnings remove the claim of ignorance: the honour sought among disbelievers was already warned against by the very messengers whose lineage includes Moses directly addressed. The next verse sets the standing witness behind the sending: God bears witness to what He sent down to you — He sent it down with His knowledge — and the angels bear witness, and God suffices as Witness (4:166).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:166

> Yet ˹if you are denied, O Prophet,˺ Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you—He has sent it with His knowledge. The angels too bear witness. And Allah ˹alone˺ is sufficient as a Witness

**God Bears Witness to What He Sent Down to You**

The verse opens *lākini Allāhu yashhadu bi-mā anzala ilayka* — yet God bears witness, testifies, to what He has sent down to you. *Yet* was explained as the reply within *so that humanity has no excuse after the messengers* (4.165): if, after that, they deny you, the denial meets God's own testimony. *Bears witness to what He sent down to you* was explained as that the whole sūrah's content — the lineage of revelation (4:163), the messengers told and untold, Moses' direct speech (4:164), the purpose of removing excuse (4:165) — is witnessed by Him who sent it, the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth (4:126). *Sent down to you* was read as the Qur'an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — and every instruction in it: the orphan women already recited (4:127), the settlement best (4:128), the share of each heir (4:11–12) — all are what He sent down. The sūrah has warned that if you disobey, to Him still belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth, and He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131): to deny the One who bears witness is to deny the Owner to whom all belongs.

**He Sent It Down With His Knowledge — and the Angels Bear Witness**

The detail *anzalahu bi-ʿilmih* — He sent it down with His knowledge — was explained as that the Book's contents — the limits, the trusts, the prayer at fixed times, settlement best, the faith that accepts all messengers — are known to Him who knows what is in hearts (4:63), is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108), and is All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134): revelation is not arbitrary but knowledge made text. *And the angels bear witness* was explained as the second testimony: the angels nearest to God who are not too proud to serve Him (4:172) — who record (4:81), who take souls asking *what were you doing?* (4:97) — witness to what He sent down. Early reports linked this to the People of the Book who denied the Prophet's ﷺ prophethood after demanding a book from heaven (4:153): the verse says the angels witness the Book sent down to you as they witnessed the truth of what came before — while the demanders demanded spectacle. The sūrah has shown that the messengers told and untold are many — *with Him are both rewards; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:134) — the angels witness to both the told and the untold.

**And God Alone Suffices as Witness**

The seal *wa kafā bi Allāhi shahīdā* — and God suffices, is enough, as Witness — was explained with *shahīd* — Witness — the same word as the witness brought from every community and the Prophet ﷺ against his (4:41), and Jesus as witness against them (4:159): above all stands the Sufficient Witness. *God suffices as Witness* was read as that where the People of the Book demand a book from heaven as sign (4:153), where the hypocrites desire a way between by distinguishing (4:150), and where night plotters hide from people while He is with them (4:108) — His witness settles all. The phrase completed the sūrah's sequence of sufficiency: sufficient as Guardian and Helper (4:45), sufficient as Trustee (4:132) — sufficient as Witness; to be the sufficient Witness is to be the Guarantor on whom judgment by the Book (4:105) rests.

**A Verse That Follows No-Excuse With Sufficient Witness**

Placed after *messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity has no excuse after the messengers; He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:165), this verse follows no-excuse with the sufficient witness: if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent down — with His knowledge — the angels bear witness — and He alone suffices as Witness. The sūrah has traced the compelling proof — given to Moses (4:153), given over the double-faced (4:91), warned against handing against yourselves (4:144); witness is the warrant that makes proof true. The sūrah that asks *whose word is more truthful than God's?* (4:122) — none — says His testimony is the most truthful. For the weak this is an opening: where you were told to verify reports through the Messenger and those in authority (4:83), to be sure before fighting (4:94), and to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), the verification that your standing rests on is His witness and the angels' — sufficient — so that you need not hang between neither these nor those (4:143), waiting to see.

**The Knowledge With Which He Sent Down Explains the Law's Detail**

The phrase *with His knowledge* was explained to keep the law's detail intelligible: the inheritance shares (4:11–12), the dowry given or graciously waived (4:4), the marriage of the bondwoman with her people's permission and her dowry (4:25), settlement best though greed persists (4:128), no total inclining (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130) — all are *with His knowledge*, not guess. Where the sūrah says He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, and turn in mercy, being All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:26–28) — His knowledge is that clarity. The next verse sets the verdict on those who reject the Sufficient Witness: those who disbelieve and hinder from God's way have strayed far astray (4:167) — far, because the witness was sufficient and delivered with knowledge.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:167

> Those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah have certainly strayed far away

**Those Who Disbelieve and Hinder From God's Way — Far Astray**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdā* — surely those who disbelieve and hinder, bar, others from God's way have certainly strayed far away. *Disbelieved* was explained as the denial after the messengers removed every excuse (4:165) and after the sufficient witness — God with His knowledge and the angels (4:166). *And hinder from God's way* was explained with *ṣadd* — to block, bar — the same hindering as *We forbade them good things for their wrongdoing and for hindering many from God's way* (4:160): there the hindering was of the People of the Book; here it is generalised to all who disbelieve and block. *God's way* was read as the noble ways He wills to make clear (4:26), the believers' path not to be left (4:115), the straight path He guides to through grace (4:175), the Book sent with truth to judge by what He shows (4:105) — all are His way. *Have certainly strayed far away* was explained as far straying — the same seal as *whoever associates others with God has strayed far astray* (4:116) and *whoever denies God, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has gone far astray* (4:136): to disbelieve and hinder is that same far. Early reports linked hindering to those who concealed the Prophet's ﷺ description, to the allies of disbelievers sought for honour (4:139), and to those who sat where revelation was mocked (4:140): hindering is doctrinal concealment and social company alike.

**A Verse That Follows No-Excuse and Sufficient Witness With Far Straying**

Placed after *messengers delivering good news and warnings, so humanity has no excuse after the messengers* (4:165) and *God bears witness… the angels too bear witness… God suffices as Witness* (4:166), this verse follows no-excuse and sufficient witness with the verdict on those who disbelieve and hinder: they have strayed far. The sequence — lineage (4:163), told and untold messengers, Moses addressed directly (4:164), purpose so no excuse (4:165), sufficient witness (4:166) — ends in the straying of those who reject it all. The sūrah has said grace is not by wishes (4:123) and both rewards are with Him (4:134): to hinder from His way is to hinder from both rewards where both are with Him who owns the heavens and earth (4:126). Elsewhere *whoever earns sin earns it only against himself* (4:111) — but hindering adds the misguidance of others to the earnings, therefore *far*.

**Disbelief Alone and Disbelief Plus Hindering**

The pairing — disbelieved, and hindered — was explained as two degrees: disbelief alone is straying; disbelief plus hindering is far straying. As *whoever commits evil will be recompensed with it* (4:123), disbelief alone is recompensed with itself; hindering adds to it, as throwing sin on the innocent adds slander to sin (4:112). The forbidding of good foods came for wrongdoing plus much hindering (4:160) — double cause, double measure; here far straying is sealed for disbelief plus hindering. The sūrah's household law confirms the pairing: hindering the suspended from her right (4:129) is the household form of *ṣadd*, and settlement (4:128) is its opposite. For the weak this is protective: where you are hindered — the helpless who could not find a way (4:98) — the far straying is declared to be the hinderer's, not yours.

**The Hinderer's Far Straying as Warning for the Community**

The hindering was described as not only blocking by force but by example: to disbelieve and claim closed hearts, to slander Mary, to boast of killing the Messiah, to take interest though forbidden — all hinder the many who observe. The sūrah has taught that counselling charity, kindness, and reconciliation for His pleasure earns a great reward (4:114) — the opposite of hindering; the hinderer's work undoes that good by making God's way seem blocked. Early commentators noted that hindering after sufficient witness (4:166) is worse than hindering before it, because the testimony — God's, with knowledge, and the angels' — has already declared the way true. That is why the seal is *far*: the distance from truth after truth was made near by messengers of good news and warning.

**Far Astray After Knowledge Was Made Clear**

The *far* was explained as distance after clarity: where He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, and turn in mercy (4:26–28), clarity came by messengers — so straying after it is far, because the clarity was great. The sūrah's coming statement that *the Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of God, nor the angels nearest* (4:172) shows that hindering from God's way includes calling to the worship of beings beside Him (4:117) and taking Satan as guardian (4:119) — far from servanthood. The verse generalises the coming warning not to go to extremes in religion (4:171): extremity is hindering, and far straying is its end. The next verse seals that straying: those who disbelieve and act unjustly — God will neither forgive them nor guide them to a path — except the path of Hell, abiding in it forever, and that is easy for God (4:168–169).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:168

> Those who disbelieve and wrong themselves—surely Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path

**Those Who Disbelieve and Act Unjustly — Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū lam yakun Allāhu li-yaghfira lahum wa lā li-yahdiyahum ṭarīqā* — surely those who disbelieve and act unjustly, wrongfully — God will not forgive them nor guide them to any path. *Disbelieved* and *acted unjustly* was explained as disbelief plus *ẓulm*: disbelief plus hindering from God's way (4:167) is the wronging of selves and others — as *whoever commits evil or wrongs himself* (4:110) and *whoever earns sin earns it only against himself* (4:111) show, wronging here exceeds the self. *God will not forgive them* was explained with forgiveness withheld where gratitude and faith would have removed any need of punishment (4:147) — here disbelief and wrong persist. *Nor guide them to any path* was read as no guidance to a *ṭarīq* — road — the same way as the believers' path (4:115) and the noble ways He guides to (4:26): to be guided to no path is to be left as *whoever God leaves to stray, you will never find a way for him* (4:88, 4:143). The sūrah has shown that *those who believed then disbelieved, then believed, then increased* (4:137) — neither forgiven nor guided to the Right Way — there the oscillation's increase removed forgiveness and guidance; here disbelief plus injustice does.

**A Verse That Follows Far Straying With Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

Placed after *those who disbelieve and hinder from God's way have certainly strayed far away* (4:167), this verse follows far straying with neither forgiveness nor guidance — except Hell's path, as the next verse adds. The sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven, though what is less than it is, for whom He wills (4:116); those who disbelieve and wrong combine disbelief, hindering, and injustice — so what is withheld is not the lesser forgiveness. The principle *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative* (4:147) shows that forgiveness is withheld here because gratitude and faith are absent, while disbelief and wrong persist. The reminder that *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134) shows that guidance to a path is with Him who owns the heavens and earth (4:126) and suffices as Trustee (4:132): to be guided to no path is to fall outside that trusteeship. Where the sūrah warns *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?* (4:144), injustice plus disbelief is the warrant for not forgiving and not guiding.

**The Two Gifts Denied — Forgiveness and Guidance**

The two denials — will not forgive, nor guide to a path — were explained as the Book's two gifts withheld: the forgiveness that effaces — *ʿAfuww* — and the guidance that shows the way. The promise that *whoever wrongs himself then seeks forgiveness finds God All-Forgiving* (4:110) shows that forgiveness is denied here where seeking is absent; and *had grace not preserved you, they would have deceived you — yet they deceive only themselves* (4:113) shows guidance denied where deception persists. That *Gardens come for those who believe and do good* (4:122) ties forgiveness to the Gardens and guidance to the straight path He guides to through grace (4:175): to deny both is to close both doors. For the weak this is clarifying: the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were those who could not find a way — forgiveness and guidance were hoped for them; here the case is the opposite — the able, disbelieving, wronging, hindering.

**The Path Not Granted Is Any Path Toward Mercy**

The phrase *nor guide them to any path* — with the indefinite *ṭarīqā*, any way — was explained as no path toward mercy remaining: the straight path to which He guides through grace (4:175) is the only road to the Gardens; to be guided to no path is to be guided not there. The declaration that *He can remove you, O humanity, and bring others* (4:133) frames removal as what remains where no path remains; and *whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than the believers' path — We let him pursue what he chose, then burn* (4:115) shows that being left to a chosen path is not being guided to the true one. The next verse names the only remaining way — the path of Hell, to abide in it forever — and adds: and that is easy for God (4:169).

**A Short Verse That Holds the Gate Open One Sentence**

Though brief — *those who disbelieve and act unjustly — God will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path* — the verse holds the gate open one sentence: except Hell's path, as the next verse states. The sūrah's pattern holds — the lowest depth without helper except those who repent (4:145–146) — but the exception is not asserted here, because disbelief and injustice persist. The coming warning not to go to extremes in religion (4.171) shows that extremity — the Trinity claim, the boast of killing the Messiah — belongs among those who disbelieve and wrong: persisting there, no forgiveness or guidance is promised, and Hell's path remains the only one left — whose ease for God underscores that mercy elsewhere is wide for the grateful and faithful (4:147).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:169

> except that of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever. And that is easy for Allah

**Except the Path of Hell — To Stay There Forever**

The verse completes *illā ṭarīqa Jahannama khālidīna fīhā abadā* — except the path of Hell, to stay, abide, in it forever and ever. *Except the path of Hell* was explained as the only road to which those who disbelieve and wrong — not forgiven, not guided to any path (4:168) — will be directed: Hell's way. *Ṭarīq* — path — was read against the sūrah's path language: the noble ways He wills to make clear (4:26), the believers' path not to be left (4:115), far straying for disbelief plus hindering (4:167) — now the path given is Hell's, as *whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than the believers' path — We let him pursue what he chose, then burn* (4:115): the burning is that path. *Staying therein forever and ever* carried the double emphasis — *khālidīn* and *abadan* — the same doubling used for the Gardens of those who believe and do good (4:122) — now for Hell, where *they will have Hell as home and find no escape* (4:121). The sūrah has shown the humiliating punishment prepared for the true disbelievers (4:151) and the lowest depth of Fire without helper (4:145) — the path's place and measure. *Forever and ever* was linked to the sūrah's promises: forever belongs to each destination — Gardens forever for belief and good; here, forever for disbelief and wrong — the only path left is lasting.

**And That Is Easy for God**

The seal *wa kāna dhālika ʿalā Allāhi yasīrā* — and that is easy, light, for God — was explained with *yasīr* — easy, not burdensome — the same word as *whoever does this unjustly, We will burn him in a Fire, and that is easy for God* (4:30). *Easy for God* was read as that His power is not constrained: He can remove humanity and bring others — He is Most Capable (4:133) — so guiding to Hell's path is easy. The sūrah has shown He is Almighty, All-Wise, who raised Jesus (4:158), sent messengers so no excuse remains (4:165), and bears witness with His knowledge (4.166) — His might makes the threat certain where He is denied. The phrase was linked to *Gardens forever, where the promise is ever true* (4:122): both Gardens and Hell forever rest with Him who encompasses everything (4.126) — the promise is as true as the threat.

**A Verse That Completes Neither-Forgiven-Nor-Guided**

Placed after *those who disbelieve and act unjustly — God will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path* (4:168), this verse completes the sentence: except Hell's path, to stay forever — and that is easy for Him. The litany — from the demand for a book from heaven (4:153) through thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing, sealed hearts, denial, slander of Mary, the boast of killing one never killed, the raising, belief before death, forbidden foods for wrongdoing and hindering, ribā, unjust consumption, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, great reward for the grounded, the lineage, the told and untold messengers, the direct speech, the good news and warnings, the sufficient witness, far straying, neither forgiven nor guided — now ends at Hell's path forever, easy for Him: where excuse was removed and witness was sufficient, the only remaining path for the persisting is stated plainly. For the weak this is an anchor: the helpless who hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were not those who disbelieved and wronged, but those who could find no way — Hell's path is for hinderers and wrongers, not for the helpless; the ease for Him is not arbitrary but measured.

**The Only Path Left Is Hell's**

The word *except* was explained to keep Hell's path as the only road left, where any other road would be mercy and guidance; to be directed to Hell's path is not guidance to mercy but letting pursue what was chosen (4:115) — the sūrah's leaving to stray (4:88, 4:143). The sūrah has shown *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134): Hell's path forever is the opposite of the other reward; the Gardens' true promise (4:122) is the guided path, Hell forever the allowed stray. The verse generalises the sūrah's *easy* — as the Fire for unjust wealth was easy for Him (4:30) — devouring wealth, ribā, and unjust consumption (4:161) are as easy to punish as everything is encompassed to know. The next passage turns from the history's litigants to humanity itself: O humanity, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good; if you disbelieve — to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth; He is All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:170) — belief's call, where Hell's easy path is the alternative.

**A Short Verse That Anchors the Certain Threat**

Though brief — *except the path of Hell, to stay there forever and ever — and that is easy for God* — the verse anchors the certain threat after far straying was declared (4:167) and neither-forgiven-nor-guided was stated (4:168). The sūrah's coming warning not to go to extremes in religion (4:171) — the Trinity claim — shows that excess belongs among those whose only remaining path is Hell forever; the correction follows immediately. The next verses address humanity and the People of the Book directly: the Messenger has come with truth (4:170); do not go to extremes (4.171); the Messiah would never disdain servitude, nor the angels nearest (4:172) — all the alternative path: belief and good, mercy and grace, the straight path (4:174–175) — versus Hell's ease.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:170

> O humanity! The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good. But if you disbelieve, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise

**O Humanity — the Messenger Has Come to You With the Truth From Your Lord**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā an-nāsu qad jāʾakumu ar-rasūlu bi-al-ḥaqqi min rabbikum* — O humanity, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord. *O humanity* was explained as the sūrah's great humanity addresses returning: *O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul* (4:1); *O humanity, if He wills He can remove you and bring others* (4:133) — now, *O humanity, the Messenger has come with the truth*. *Has certainly come to you the Messenger* was read as the chain's arrival: revelation sent as to Noah and the prophets after him (4:163), messengers told and untold, Moses spoken to directly (4:164), all bearers of good news and warnings so no excuse remains (4:165), the sufficient witness to what He sent down with His knowledge (4:166) — the Messenger is the told messenger come to them. *With the truth* was explained as that he came with true content and true origin, as the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105), and as God's promise is ever true (4:122). *From your Lord* was read as from the Owner of the heavens and earth (4:126), the Lord who created from a single soul (4:1): truth from Him.

**So Believe — It Is Better for You**

The call *fa-āminū khayran lakum* — so believe; it is better for you, good for you — was explained with *better for you* — for the addressee, not for Him: He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131), to Him still belongs all though you disbelieve. *Believe* was read as comprehensive faith — *have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — steadfast, not wavering, not distinguishing between God and His messengers desiring a way between (4:150) — to be among those who accept all and reject none, who are given their rewards (4:152). *Better for you* was linked to *Gardens forever, where the promise is ever true* (4:122), and to the great reward promised the grounded (4:162), and to those who hold fast being guided through the straight path (4:175); to believe is to obtain the emigrant's many havens (4:100) and enrichment after separation (4:130) — better for you is both this world and the Hereafter. Early reports added that the *so* makes belief the fitting response: after the Messenger has come with truth, excuse removed (4:165) and witness sufficient (4:166), belief is not speculation but answer.

**But If You Disbelieve — to God Belongs Whatever Is in the Heavens and Earth**

The warning *wa in takfurū fa-inna li Allāhi mā fī as-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — but if you disbelieve, then indeed to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth — was explained as that disbelief does not impoverish the Owner: as *We commanded those before you and you to be mindful; if you disobey, to Him still belongs all; He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131) — here *if you disbelieve* after the Messenger's truth, the same ownership stands. The clause was read against the history just told: the demand greater than a book — *show us God plainly* — was answered with thunderbolt and Mount raised (4:153–154); to disbelieve while ownership is His is the demand's end-form. The sūrah has asked *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative* (4:147): punishment is not His need; ownership after disbelief says the same — disbelief impoverishes the disbeliever, not the Owner. The clause was also linked to *except the path of Hell, to stay forever — and that is easy for Him* (4:169): Hell's easy path lies within that same belonging.

**And God Is All-Knowing, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīmā* — and God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise — was explained with *All-Knowing* — knowing belief and disbelief, knowing whether *better for you* was chosen, All-Aware of what you do (4:135) — and *All-Wise* — who sent messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse remains (4:165), raised the Mount for the covenant, and sent the Book with truth to judge (4:105): the wisdom is that the Messenger came with truth from the Lord. *All-Knowing, All-Wise* sealed the law that *whoever earns sin earns it only against himself; God is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:111): His knowing and wisdom guarantee that belief and disbelief are measured without wronging an atom (4:40) or a speck (4:124). To call all humanity to believe, for their own good, while being Self-Sufficient, All-Knowing, All-Wise, shows belief is medicine, not debt.

**A Verse That Follows Hell's Easy Path With Humanity's Call**

Placed after the whole history of demand and correction (4:153–169), this verse turns the sūrah from third-person history to second-person call: O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth — believe, for your good; if you disbelieve — to Him still belongs all — He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. The sūrah that began with a single soul now sets humanity's choice where ownership, knowledge, and wisdom guarantee that believing is better for you, not for Him. For the weak this is an opening: where you were told to refer disputes to God and the Messenger (4:59), the Messenger has come with truth — refer now; where you were told to verify reports (4:83), the truth to verify has come. The next passage addresses the People of the Book directly: do not go to extremes in your religion; say nothing about God except the truth; the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was only a messenger — God's Word through Mary and a spirit from Him; believe in God and His messengers; do not say "Three"; desist — it is better for you; God is only one God; He is far above having a son; to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth; and God suffices as Trustee (4:171).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:171

> O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith; say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit ˹created by a command˺ from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, "Trinity." Stop!—for your own good. Allah is only One God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs

**O People of the Book — Do Not Go to Extremes in Your Religion**

The verse opens *yā ahla al-kitābi lā taghlū fī dīnikum wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — O People of the Book, do not exceed limits, go to extremes, in your religion, and say nothing about God except the truth. *Do not go to extremes* — *lā taghlū* — was explained with *ghuluww* — excess beyond measure — against the two directions the sūrah has traced: the Jewish denial of the Messiah — the slander of Mary with mighty slander (4:156) and the boast of killing one never killed (4:157) — and the Christian divinising of him. To make Jesus god is excess; to deny him is neglect — both miss the truth. *Say nothing about God except the truth* was explained as that He is the Sufficient Witness (4:166) who bore witness to what He sent down with His knowledge, and whose word none exceeds in truth (4:122): to speak about God without truth is to claim a testimony you do not have. The sūrah has shown the Book sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); excess is to judge without that showing. Early reports noted that Christians exceeded concerning Jesus as some Jews exceeded in slandering Mary; the middle is the truth — Jesus is an honoured servant, not a god.

**The Messiah, Son of Mary, Was No More Than a Messenger — His Word Cast to Mary, and a Spirit From Him**

The definition *innamā al-masīḥu ʿĪsā ibnu Maryama rasūlu Allāhi wa kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama wa rūḥun minhu* — the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of God, and His Word He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him — was explained with three terms. *Messenger of God* was read as the chain's continuity: revelation sent as to Noah and the prophets after him, including Jesus (4:163), Moses spoken to directly (4:164), all messengers as good news and warnings (4:165) — Jesus is among them. *His Word He conveyed to Mary* was explained as the command *Be* — as *when He decrees a thing, He only says to it, Be, and it is* (3:47) — creation by a word, without father: the Word is command, not offspring. *A spirit from Him* was explained as the spirit *breathed into her* (66:12) — created from Him by His command, not a part of Him: what is from Him belongs to Him, as *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth* (4:171) — the spirit belongs to Him. *No more than* — *innamā* — was read as restriction: messenger, Word, spirit-from-Him — and nothing further; divinity is excluded as excess. Where the sūrah declared those who distinguish between God and messengers true disbelievers (4:151) and promised rewards to those accepting all messengers (4:152), this definition is the acceptance of Jesus as messenger among messengers.

**So Believe in God and His Messengers, and Do Not Say "Three" — Desist, It Is Better for You**

The command *fa-āminū bi Allāhi wa rusulihi wa lā taqūlū thalāthatun* — so believe in God and His messengers, and do not say "Three" — was explained with *Three* as the Trinity doctrine — the excess the sūrah names *ghuluww*. *Do not say Three* was read against the truth *God is only one God* — One — as *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth*: to say three is to divide the ownership. *Desist — it is better for you* — *intahū khayran lakum* — was explained with the same *better for you* as *O humanity, the Messenger has come with the truth — so believe, for your own good* (4:170): desisting from the Three is better for you, as He is Self-Sufficient (4:131) — not for Him. *God is only one God* was read as the sūrah's monotheism throughout: association is not forgiven (4:116); the female gods invoked besides Him were Satan's share (4:117) — the Three is association's refined form, far straying.

**Glory Be to Him — Far Above Having a Son — and He Suffices as Trustee**

The glorification *subḥānahu an yakūna lahu walad* — glory be to Him, exalted is He, that He should have a son — was explained with *subḥānahu* — the exaltation of the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131, 4:170). *That He should have a son* was read as impossibility for the Self-Sufficient who can remove humanity and bring others (4.133): a son answers no need. *To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth* was explained as that ownership denies a son's need — as stated after the Messenger's call: *if you disbelieve, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth; He is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:170); the Three divides what is His. *And God suffices as Trustee* — *kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* — was read as that the Trustee suffices without a son: as the oppressed cry for a guardian and helper from grace (4:75), the guardian is Him — not a third of three; as the sūrah said *God suffices as Trustee* (4:132), three are not needed for trusteeship.

**A Verse That Follows Humanity's Call With the People of the Book's Correction**

Placed after *O humanity, the Messenger has come with the truth, so believe for your own good… He is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:170), this verse corrects the People of the Book whose history the sūrah has just narrated — demand, thunderbolt, calf, covenant and its breaking, sealed hearts, slander of Mary, boast of killing one who was raised (4:153–158). The correction is the middle after two extremes: the Jewish extremes of denial, slander, and boasting murder, and the Christian extreme of deification as Trinity. The sūrah that began with a single soul spread into humanity (4:1) and declared *neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book* (4:123) makes this middle the truth by which it has judged throughout: the Book sent with truth, the witness sufficient (4:166). For the weak this is an opening: where settlement is best in households (4:128), the Trinity is not settlement between God and His messengers; to believe in God and His messengers and not say Three is the settlement that is best — better for you.

**The Word Through Mary as Command, Not Offspring**

The phrase *His Word He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him* was explained to distinguish the Word as *Be* — commanded, not begotten — and the spirit as created from Him, not a part of Him. The next verse proves the rank: *the Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of God, nor would the angels nearest* (4:172) — servant is the Word's own rank; what is worshipped is not. So the definition closes where the sūrah's monotheism began: one God, Owner of the heavens and earth, sufficient as Trustee.
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:172

> The Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels nearest to Allah. Those who are too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together

**The Messiah Would Never Disdain Servitude, Nor the Angels Nearest**

The verse states *lan yastankifa al-masīḥu an yakūna ʿabdan li Allāhi wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — the Messiah — Jesus, son of Mary, messenger and Word through Mary and a spirit from Him (4:171) — would never disdain, refuse out of pride, to be a servant of God, nor would the angels nearest, those brought near. *Would never disdain* was explained with *istinkāf* — pride that refuses service — the very trait of the proud who will be gathered, and of Satan, who refused to prostrate and was cursed (4:118). *To be a servant of God* was read as *ʿubūdiyyah* — servitude — the rank of every messenger in the lineage: revelation sent as to Noah and the prophets after him, including Jesus (4:163) — all are servants. *Nor the angels nearest* was explained with *muqarrabūn* — those brought near — the highest of creation: the Messiah, whose mother was slandered yet who is among the prophets (4:163), and the angels who bear witness to what He sent down with His knowledge (4:166) — all are servants. The sūrah has said *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth; He suffices as Trustee* (4:171) — servants belong to Him; to claim the Messiah stands beyond servitude is the extreme — *ghuluww* (4:171) — and the Messiah himself would never claim it: the proof of his rank is his own refusal of deification.

**Whoever Is Too Proud to Worship Him Will Be Gathered Before Him All Together**

The warning *wa man yastankif ʿan ʿibādatihi wa yastakbir fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿā* — whoever is too proud to worship Him, serve Him, and grows arrogant — He will gather, muster, them to Him, all together — was explained with the pair *too proud* and *arrogant* — the pair already seen in Satan, cursed, who claimed a share (4:118). *From His worship* was read as that worship is not debasement but honour: Abraham was taken as close friend (4:125) as a servant; Moses was spoken to directly (4:164) as a servant; the angels nearest are servants. *He will gather them to Him all together* was explained with *ḥashara* — to gather — the same gathering as *He will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt* (4:87) and *He will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) — the too proud are gathered for reckoning. *All together* was explained as that the Messiah did not disdain and the angels did not disdain — yet the proud among humanity will be gathered with the proud, as the hypocrites were gathered together in Hell.

**A Verse That Follows "Do Not Say Three" With the Messiah's Own Refusal**

Placed after *O People of the Book, do not go to extremes… the Messiah was no more than a messenger… do not say "Three"; desist — it is better for you… He is far above having a son; He suffices as Trustee* (4:171), this verse follows the prohibition with the Messiah's own attitude: he would never disdain servitude. The correction — he is but a messenger — is proven by his own refusal: to call him god is to attribute to him what he would disdain. The sūrah has shown that *Satan promises only delusion* (4:120) and his share are those who invoke beings besides God (4:117); to make the Messiah more than a servant is delusion — not his wish. The sūrah has shown *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134): servitude is the worship that receives both, as the emigrant's havens were the reward of obedient worship. For the weak this is an anchor: where the sūrah asks *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful?* (4:147) — servitude is grateful faith; to be too proud to worship is ingratitude's extreme.

**The Angels Nearest as Witness to Servitude**

The addition *nor the angels nearest* was explained as the corroborating witness: the angels nearest to Him — who bear witness to what He sent down with His knowledge (4:166), who record, who take souls asking *what were you doing?* (4:97) — are servants who were not too proud; their nearness is servitude, not partnership. The sūrah has shown that every one of the People of the Book will believe in him before his death, and on the Day he will be a witness against them (4:159): the Messiah as witness is a servant-witness, as the angels are witness-servants. Where the sūrah prohibited total inclining, leaving the other suspended (4:129), making the Messiah god is inclining entirely to a servant while leaving the One suspended; the verse corrects the inclining: the Messiah was not too proud, nor the angels — worship is for Him alone whose ownership is all (4:126). The next verse states what follows the gathering: full repayment with increase from grace for those who believe and do good — painful punishment without protector or helper for the too proud (4:173).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:173

> As for those who believe and do good, He will reward them in full and increase them out of His grace. But those who are too proud and arrogant, He will subject them to a painful punishment. And besides Allah they will find no protector or helper

**Those Who Believe and Do Good — Paid in Full and Increased From His Grace**

The verse opens *fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū aṣ-ṣāliḥāti fa-yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa yazīduhum min faḍlih* — as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their wages in full and increase them out of His grace, bounty. *Believe and do good* is the sūrah's shorthand for the faithful — opposed to the too proud who disdained worship (4:172) and those who disbelieved and strayed far (4:167). *He will pay them their wages in full* was read with *waffā* — to give in full, complete — under the sūrah's rule *God does not wrong even an atom; if it is a good deed, He multiplies it* (4:40): paying in full is not wronging even a speck (4:124) — the atom not wronged is the wage given whole. *And increase them out of His grace* was explained with *faḍl* — grace, bounty — the grace without which they would have deceived you (4:113), and *great is His favour upon you* (4:113): the increase is grace, not debt — as the Gardens forever where the promise is true (4:122): the increase is the rivers beneath, never cut. Early reports linked the increase to admission into Gardens under which rivers flow and to the emigrant's abundance (4:100) — this world and the Hereafter.

**But the Too Proud Will Be Subjected to a Painful Punishment**

The contrast *wa-ammā alladhīna istankafū wa istakbarū fa-yuʿadhdhibuhum ʿadhāban alīmā* — but as for those who were too proud and arrogant — He will punish them with a painful punishment — was explained with the same pair as the previous verse — too proud to worship, and arrogant (4:172) — now gathered to punishment. *A painful punishment* was explained with *alīm* — painful — the same adjective as the good news announced to hypocrites (4:138) and the punishment prepared for the disbelievers among the People of the Book who took ribā and consumed wealth unjustly (4:161): pain answers pride — to disdain servitude is to earn the servant-opposite's pain. The sūrah has shown the lowest depth of Fire without helper (4:145), and *neither forgiven nor guided, except Hell's path forever — and that is easy for Him* (4:168–169): the painful is where the path ends.

**And They Will Find No Protector or Helper Besides God**

The closure *wa lā yajidūna lahum min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — and they will find for themselves, besides God, no protector, guardian, nor helper — was explained with *walī* and *naṣīr* — the pair the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and God alone suffices as (4:45) — and the pair the hypocrites sought among disbeliever allies for honour (4:139): the too proud sought honour in allies and in pride itself, yet will find no guardian and no helper where the punishment falls. *Besides God* was read as that no female god invoked (4:117), no Satan taken as guardian (4:119), no disbeliever ally (4:144) will avail on the Day when all are gathered before Him together (4:172). The sūrah has said *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134): protection besides Him is unnecessary where both rewards are with Him — and to seek it is to find none. Where the sūrah declared *God suffices as Trustee* (4:171) — for the Messiah's case — the too proud find no trustee.

**A Verse That Follows the Gathering With Repayment and Punishment**

Placed after *the Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant, nor the angels nearest; the too proud and arrogant will be gathered before Him all together* (4:172), this verse follows the gathering with the two outcomes: for those who believe and do good — wages in full and increase from grace; for the too proud — painful punishment, with no protector or helper besides Him. The sūrah has shown *whoever does good, male or female, with faith will enter Paradise, not wronged a speck* (4:124) — the wages in full are that entry; and *whoever commits evil will be recompensed with it, finding no protector besides God* (4:123) — the painful, where disbelief and wrong stand — now applied to pride. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by desires (4:27) nor let desires deviate justice (4:135) sees disdain and arrogance as the pride that deviates most — because servitude is the sūrah's ethic: standing for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is servitude; not inclining entirely, leaving a hanging (4:129), is servitude; verifying before fighting (4:94) is servitude.

**Payment in Full Is Justice; Increase Is Grace**

The phrase *pay them in full and increase them out of His grace* was explained to keep payment as justice — not wronging an atom (4:40) — and increase as grace: the grace that taught you what you did not know (4:113), and that makes *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative* (4:147) true — appreciation is increase from grace. The sūrah has shown the emigrant's many havens and abundance (4:100) and the enrichment after separation (4:130) — both are increase from His bounty. For the weak this is steadying: where settlement is best though greed persists (4:128), to be among those who believe and do good is to have wages fulfilled and grace increase; where you were too proud to worship, the wage is pain, and the protector is none. The next passage turns to humanity with its final gifts: O humanity, conclusive proof has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a brilliant light (4:174).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:174

> O humanity! There has come to you conclusive evidence from your Lord. And We have sent down to you a brilliant light

**O Humanity — Conclusive Proof Has Come From Your Lord**

The verse states *yā ayyuhā an-nāsu qad jāʾakum burhānun min rabbikum* — O humanity, there has certainly come to you a proof, conclusive evidence, demonstration, from your Lord. *O humanity* was explained as the sūrah's great addresses returning: *O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul* (4:1); *O humanity, He can remove you and bring others* (4:133); *O humanity, the Messenger has come with the truth — so believe, for your own good* (4:170) — now: conclusive proof has come. *Has certainly come to you* was read with emphasis: the proof has arrived, not pending — the lineage from Noah through the prophets to you (4:163), the messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse remains (4:165), the sufficient witness (4:166) — the proof stands. *Proof from your Lord* was explained with *burhān* — conclusive demonstration — the same clarity as His will to make clear (4:26) and teaching what you did not know (4:113): the *burhān* was explained as the Prophet ﷺ himself, with his miracles and his Call. Early reports linked the *proof* to the Messenger, and the *light* that follows to the Qur'an — two gifts: messenger and Book. The sūrah has shown *to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth; He is Fully Aware* (4:126): proof from the Lord who owns and encompasses is the nearest possible proof. The phrase was linked to *Gardens for those who believe and do good* (4:122): the proof's purpose is the Gardens — as *so believe, for your own good* (4:170).

**And We Have Sent Down to You a Clear Light**

The second clause *wa anzalnā ilaykum nūran mubīnā* — and We have sent down to you a clear, brilliant, manifest light — was explained with *nūr* — light — *mubīn* — clear — the same *mubīn* as the compelling proof Moses was given (4:153). *We sent down to you* was read as the Qur'an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — light that shows judgment, as the Mount raised (4:154) was proof made visible. *A clear light* was explained as the Qur'an that makes clear, as He wills to lighten burdens (4:28) — light lightens; the prayer written at fixed times (4:103) is that light's schedule. Early reports added that the proof and the light are the two witnesses of the preceding passage: God bears witness with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness (4:166) — His knowledge is the light; the witnessed sending is the proof. Where the sūrah warned not to go to extremes — say nothing about God except the truth; do not say Three (4:171) — the light is what makes excess visible as excess, as Satan's promising only delusion (4:120) is darkness.

**A Verse That Follows Humanity's Call With Its Complement**

Placed after the Messenger's call (4:170), the People of the Book's correction (4:171), the Messiah's refusal of deification (4:172), and the repayment and punishment (4:173), this verse follows with the complement: conclusive proof has come from your Lord — the Messenger — and a clear light sent down — the Qur'an. The sūrah has shown those who disbelieve and hinder straying far (4:167) and the unjust unforgiven, unguided except Hell's path (4:168–169); light is the opposite of hindering — to send light is to unblock the way. The sūrah that allows no good counsel except charity, kindness, and reconciliation (4:114) — the light is counsel made good: the Book's light is charity. For the weak this is an opening: where settlement is best (4:128), the light shows settlement; where the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99), the light shows the pardon; where the emigrant finds many havens (4:100), the light shows the havens.

**The Clear Light That Makes Error Visible**

The phrase *a clear light* was explained to include the light's work: it makes the Three visible as excess (4:171), the slander against Mary visible as mighty slander (4:156), the boast of killing the un-killed visible as assumption (4:157), ribā taken despite prohibition visible as unjust consumption (4:161). The sūrah has asked *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative* (4:147) — light is gratitude's tool: to be grateful, you must see what He gave — the light shows it. The verse generalises the sūrah's *He wills to make clear* (4:26): the proof and the light are that making clear. The next verse describes those who respond to it: those who believe in God and hold fast to Him — admitted into mercy from Him and grace, guided to Himself by a straight path (4:175).

**A Short Verse That Anchors Evidence Before Guidance**

Though brief — *O humanity, conclusive proof has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light* — the verse anchors the evidence before the guidance is stated. The chapter that began with a single soul (4:1) has shown ownership, trusteeship, capability to replace, both rewards, justice against selves, comprehensive faith, the hypocrite portrait, the lowest depth except for the repentant, the discipline of speech, the distinction refused, the long litany of demand and correction, the forbidden foods, the grounded rewarded, the lineage, the told and untold messengers, the direct speech, the good news and warnings, the sufficient witness, far straying, Hell's easy path, humanity's call, the People of the Book's correction, the Messiah's servitude — now: proof and light have come, so that excuse is cut where light shines. The next verses give the response and the sūrah's final ruling: hold fast and be guided to Himself by a straight path (4:175); and the ruling about the *kalālah* — the one who dies without parent or child (4:176).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:175

> As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the Straight Path

**Those Who Believe in God and Hold Fast to Him — Admitted Into Mercy and Grace**

The verse states *fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū bi Allāhi wa iʿtaṣamū bihi fa-sa-yudkhiluhum fī raḥmatin minhu wa faḍl* — as for those who believe in God and hold fast, cling, to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and grace, bounty. *Believe in God* was explained as comprehensive faith — God, His Messenger, the Book, the Scriptures, the angels, the Last Day (4:136) — steadfast, not distinguishing among messengers (4:150–152) — the faith that accepts all whose stories were told and untold (4:164). *And hold fast to Him* was read with *iʿtiṣām* — holding fast — the same holding fast required of the repentant hypocrites (4:146), and practiced by the well-grounded who establish prayer (4:162), and by the emigrant whose reward is secured upon God (4:100). *To Him* was explained as both: to God and to His rope — the Qur'an, the clear light and conclusive proof just sent down (4:174), the Book sent with truth to judge between people (4:105). *He will admit them into mercy from Him and grace* was explained with *raḥmah* — mercy — and *faḍl* — grace — the two that make the Gardens true (4:122): mercy as forgiveness of faults, grace as increase beyond them. The sūrah has asked *why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative* (4:147): admission into mercy and grace is the Appreciative's answer to holding fast. Where *with Him are both rewards; He hears and sees* (4:134) — mercy and grace are those rewards.

**And Guide Them to Himself by a Straight Path**

The second promise *wa yahdīhim ilayhi ṣirāṭan mustaqīmā* — and He will guide them to Himself by a straight, upright, direct path — was explained with *guide them to Himself* — not only to the Gardens but to Him, as the emigrant emigrates to God and His Messenger (4:100) and the reward falls upon Him. *A straight path* was explained as the sūrah's path: the noble ways He wills to make clear (4:26), the believers' path not to be left (4:115), now the straight path He guides to through His mercy and grace. *Straight* was read as the opposite of extremes — *ghuluww* (4:171): the Trinity and the denial both deviate; straight is the middle — the Messiah a servant and messenger, not a god; Mary pure, not slandered; Moses spoken to directly — the truth. The sūrah has shown *the Messiah would never disdain to be a servant* (4:172): servitude is the straight path; disdain is the deviation. *Guide them to Himself* was linked to *Gardens under which rivers flow forever, where the promise is ever true* (4:122): the Gardens are mercy and grace, guided to Him.

**A Verse That Follows Evidence and Light With Response**

Placed after *O humanity, conclusive proof has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light* (4:174), this verse follows evidence and light with response: those who believe in God and hold fast to Him — to that proof and light — He will admit into mercy and grace and guide to Himself by a straight path. The sūrah has shown the opposite: those who disbelieve and hinder stray far (4:167); the unjust are neither forgiven nor guided except Hell's path forever (4:168–169). The sūrah that warns against allies instead of believers (4:144) and describes the lowest depth without helper (4:145) makes holding fast to Him the opposite alliance — taking Him as the Trustee who suffices (4:132). For the weak this is steadying: where disputes are referred to God and the Messenger (4:59), holding fast is the referral; where reports are verified (4:83), the proof and light are the verification; where certainty is required before fighting (4:94), holding fast is the certainty.

**Mercy and Grace, Guided by the Straight Path**

The pair *mercy from Him and grace* was explained as mercy that pardons the helpless (4:99) and forgives the mistaken (4:92) — Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving — and grace that gives the emigrant many havens and abundance (4:100), the grounded a great reward (4:162), and the doers of good wages in full with increase (4:173). *He will guide them to Himself by a straight path* was linked to the sūrah's will to make clear, guide to noble ways, and turn in mercy (4:26–28): the making clear is the proof and light (4:174); the guiding to noble ways is the straight path; the turning in mercy is mercy from Him and grace. To be guided to Him by the straight path is to be among those who believe and do good in the Gardens where the promise is true (4:122) — and the straight path is the sūrah's whole law: orphans, women, inheritance, trusts, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham's way, settlement, enrichment — all straight.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Holding Fast Before the Final Ruling**

Though brief — *as for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself by a straight path* — the verse anchors holding fast before the sūrah's final ruling. The chapter that began with a single soul and honouring ties (4.1) closes its creed here: believe, hold fast to the proof and light, and be guided to Him — and then gives its last law.
