The next verse is that ruling: they ask you for a decision concerning the *kalālah* — the one who dies without parent or child — God decides for you: the sister's half, the brother's all, the two sisters' two-thirds, the male's share equal to two females — God makes it clear so you do not go astray, and He has knowledge of everything (4:176).
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:176

> They ask you ˹for a ruling, O Prophet˺. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents." If a man dies childless and leaves behind a sister, she will inherit one-half of his estate, whereas her brother will inherit all of her estate if she dies childless. If this person leaves behind two sisters, they together will inherit two-thirds of the estate. But if the deceased leaves male and female siblings, a male's share will be equal to that of two females. Allah makes ˹this˺ clear to you so you do not go astray. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things

**They Ask You for a Ruling Concerning the Kalālah**

The verse opens *yastaftūnaka qul Allāhu yuftīkum fī al-kalālah* — they ask you, seek your ruling — say: God gives you a ruling concerning the *kalālah* — the one who dies leaving neither child nor parent. *They ask you* was explained as the sūrah's second formal asking, after *they ask you concerning women; say, God gives you a ruling concerning them* (4:127) — there, orphan women and helpless children; here, the estate of the one whose line is cut at both ends. *Say, God gives you a ruling* was read as that ruling belongs to the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth, Fully Aware of everything (4:126) — and as the proof and light have come from your Lord (4:174): the ruling is light. *Kalālah* was explained with its root — *kull*, the whole — the one whose inheritance will pass to the whole kin-group because neither ascendant nor descendant survives, whose estate therefore falls to the siblings — extending the rule already begun for siblings in 4:12 — *if a man or woman leaves neither parents nor children but has a brother or sister, each of them gets a sixth* — there for the maternal sibling; here elaborated for the full and paternal siblings. Early reports noted this verse was among the last revealed, answering the case of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who fell ill as a *kalālah* without parent or child and asked about his sisters' shares — the sūrah's closing ruling is personal: the family's ties at the edge of death.

**If a Man Dies Childless Leaving a Sister — Her Half; and He Inherits All of Her**

The detail *in imruʾun halāka laysa lahu waladun wa lahu ukhtun fa lahā niṣfu mā taraka wa huwa yarithuhā in lam yakun lahā walad* — if a man dies having no child, and he has a sister, then she has half of what he leaves, and he inherits from her if she has no child — was explained as two mirrored rulings. The *kalālah* man with one surviving sister: she inherits half — after the fulfilment of bequests and debts (4:11–12), as all obligatory shares are — matching the single daughter's half (4:11): one female alone, half. The mirror: a woman who dies childless leaving a brother — he inherits her entire estate — *wa huwa yarithuhā* — and he inherits her, all of it. The imbalance between her half and his all was read against the sūrah's principle: where heirs are together, *the male has the share of two females* (4:11, and below), because *men are maintainers of women from what God has given some over others and what they spend from their wealth* (4:34) — inheritance corresponds to expenditure. Where no descendant remains, the brother assumes the clan's protection that the deceased's line would have given; as the single soul spread into humanity (4:1), the brother's whole inheritance sustains the ties. The sūrah has shown inheritance is *a decree from God* (4:11) and that keeping God's limits admits to Gardens (4:13) while transgressing them casts into Fire (4:14) — the *kalālah* shares are those limits.

**If There Are Two Sisters — Two-Thirds**

The case *fa-in kānatā ithnatayni fa-lahumā ath-thuluthāni mimmā taraka* — but if the two are two sisters, then they have two-thirds of what he leaves — was explained with *ithnatayn* — two sisters together — matching *if only daughters, two or more, their share is two-thirds* (4.11): the female pair shares the daughters' two-thirds. *Of what he leaves* was read after bequests and debts without harm to heirs (4:12). Two-thirds leaves the remaining third to other kin where present — the light of the ruling (*God makes it clear*, below) assigns each their portion. The sūrah has shown that shares are decreed for men and women, small or large, obligatory (4:7); that orphan women deprived yet desired are protected (4:127); that helpless children are stood for with justice (4:127) — the *kalālah* sisters are that justice applied at death's edge, when neither child nor parent remains to them.

**If the Heirs Are Brothers and Sisters — the Male Has the Share of Two Females**

The general rule *wa-in kānū ikhwatan rijālan wa nisāʾan fa-li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi al-unthayayn* — but if the heirs are brothers and sisters, male and female together, then the male has the share of two females — was explained with the mixed sibling group as the decisive case: among the *kalālah* heirs, the sūrah's arithmetic — *the male's share is like the share of two females* — the same rule as among children (4:11). The principle was read as inheritance corresponding to provision: *men are maintainers of women* from what God gave them and what they spend (4:34) — where brothers carry the expenditure, the share is doubled; where sisters inherit alone, they take half or two-thirds whole. The sūrah has shown that whoever does good, male or female, with faith enters Paradise, not wronged a speck (4.124): Paradise knows no doubling — there, deeds alone are weighed; the doubling is the world's division, tracking the world's burden. The rule was linked to *Gardens forever, where the promise is ever true* (4:122): the world's shares, accepted as *better for you* (4:170), are the light's own division.

**God Makes This Clear So You Do Not Go Astray — and He Knows Everything**

The seal *yubayyinu Allāhu lakum an taḍillū wa Allāhu bi-kulli shayʾin ʿalīm* — God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, and God has knowledge of everything — was explained with *He makes clear to you* — the same clarity as His will to make clear and guide to noble ways and turn in mercy (4:26), the same *mubīn* as the clear light (4:174): now even the *kalālah* is made clear. *Lest you go astray* was read as that inheritance without clarity becomes injustice and hindering from God's way (4:160) — the wrongs for which blessings were forfeited; to make clear is to prevent the straying that disputes over the dead so easily become. *God has knowledge of everything* was explained with *everything* — as He is Fully Aware, encompassing all (4:126) — He who counts every child and sister and brother, every bequest and debt without harm — the Owner of the heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131) knows the *kalālah* shares. The sūrah that began with the single soul spread into humanity and ties to be honoured (4:1) ends with the ties' shares at death, where a single soul's line is cut at both ends — yet the ties remain as siblings, and God makes clear so you do not stray, as He is knowing of all.

**A Verse That Follows Evidence and Light With Inheritance Made Clear**

Placed after the conclusive proof and clear light (4:174) and the straight path for those who hold fast (4:175), this verse follows with inheritance made clear: the ruling for the *kalālah* — one sister's half, the brother's all, two sisters' two-thirds, mixed siblings by the two-to-one rule — God makes it clear so you do not go astray; He knows everything. The sūrah that promised those who hold fast the straight path (4:175) shows the straight path's concreteness: shares assigned, disputes pre-empted, the orphaned and the heirless protected by numbers fixed from heaven. The chapter that opened with creation from a single soul and the honour due to wombs (4:1) — and wound through orphans' wealth, marriage, inheritance, trusts, fear-prayer, judgment, hypocrisy, the People of the Book's litany, the Messiah's true rank, the proof and light — ends where families end: with what remains, divided by the One who knows everything. For the weak this is the closing assurance: where helpless children were stood for (4:127) and sisters deprived yet desired were protected (4:127), the heirless sisters now stand before fixed shares — half, two-thirds, or beside brothers at two-to-one — all made clear lest you stray, by the One whose earth is spacious and promise true, who is Appreciative, All-Knowing, Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Fully Aware, encompassing everything.
